en: The Briefly Extracted Recitation Sūtra from the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
For the benefit of all sentient beings, so that they may attain the three bodies,
I take refuge and pay homage to the Three Jewels with body, speech, and mind in harmony.
To the one whose vajra body, speech, and mind pervade the triple world,
who is able to act as the sovereign lord, and who expounds the Vajradhātu—
to him I prostrate with my whole being.
The heroic and fierce Akṣobhya, who has subdued all māras;
he is the most supreme manifestation of jewels, and he honors the Dharma according to reality;
he who accomplishes the non-empty—homage to Vajrasattva.
To the one who benefits sentient beings;
to the one who bestows empowerment, the Treasury of Space;
to the protector Mahāvalokiteśvara; and to those born from yoga; I pay homage.
O Secret Viśvakarman, with a sincere heart I pay you full homage.

Now, within this *Vajraśekhara-mahāyogatantra-rāja* consisting of one hundred thousand verses, for the sake of practitioners of yoga to accomplish the methods of yoga, I shall briefly explain the most supreme secret dharma of reality as encompassed by all Tathāgatas.
"Any who wish to practice and possess wisdom should clearly understand the true mantra methods of the samaya;
having received empowerment from a venerable ācārya within the various maṇḍalas, they shall purify their bodies,
be free from fear, possess profound and great fortitude, and be well-disciplined in mind and courageous in resolve."
Being free from cowardice, respectful and reverent, pleasing to all who behold him, compassionate toward all beings,
constantly practicing generosity, abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, and delighting in the bodhicitta—
one who possesses such virtues should rely upon the teacher’s instructions and diligently cultivate offerings; he should guard the samaya so as not to let it decline.
Those who have not fallen away from their practice; who do not give rise to contempt for the Vajrācārya;
who do not act as evil friends toward their fellow students; who give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings; who never grow weary of or abandon the bodhicitta;
and who possess various kinds of wisdom and merit within all maṇḍala rituals—such persons are permitted to enter.
Regarding the methods for recitation, performing homa, receiving empowerment, and so forth:
"In this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, the method for introducing the vajra-disciples is taught.
Among these, those who enter the maṇḍala do so for the sake of protecting, benefiting, and bringing happiness to the entire realm of sentient beings, thereby accomplishing the most supreme task."
Regarding those who should enter this great maṇḍala, one should not discriminate between those who are worthy vessels and those who are not. Why is this?
World-Honored One!

There may be sentient beings who have committed great transgressions; yet once they behold this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, or enter it, all their karmic obstructions and hindrances shall be completely removed.
“World-Honored One!
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are deeply attached to all manner of wealth, food, drink, and sensual pleasures; they loathe the samaya and are not diligent in making offerings.”
Those individuals who enter this maṇḍala and perform their activities according to their wishes shall have all their aspirations fully realized.

“World-Honored One, there may be sentient beings who, for the sake of pleasure in music, song, dance, and food, act according to their whims; because they do not understand the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas and lack inquiry into the Dharma, they enter the temples and maṇḍalas of other externalist deities.”

"For the sake of accomplishing all that is sought, regarding the precepts of the maṇḍala of all Tathāgata families, the task of gathering in sentient beings, and that which can produce unsurpassed love and joy—those who do not enter these because of fear and dread, even those who have entered the paths of the maṇḍalas of the evil destinies, are likewise capable of entering the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu."

"In order to attain the supreme accomplishment of all joy and bliss, to obtain mental delight and peace, and to close the gateways to all evil destinies, one diligently practices asceticism in the stages of dhyāna, vimokṣa, and so forth; yet for those [practitioners], even upon merely entering this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas shall be obtained without difficulty."
How much more so for those who have already completed their training?

"If there are others who request the ācārya, or if the ācārya sees another person who is a fit vessel for the Dharma, free from faults, possessing vast and superior resolve, whose mental conduct is steadfast and virtuous, who is endowed with faith, and who seeks the benefit and happiness of others—having seen such a person as this, even if they do not request it, he should personally call them and say:
'O son of good family!'"
I shall explain to you the ritual procedures for the secret practices of the Mahāyāna.
Within the Mahāyāna teachings, you are a worthy vessel.

All those who were, will be, or are currently present as Protectors, remaining in the world for the benefit of beings, have all realized this secret Dharma; thus, beneath the Bodhi tree, the heroic Lion of the Śākyas attained supreme, signless omniscience by means of attaining secret yoga, whereby he shattered the great army of Māra and terrified those who cause affliction.
"Therefore, noble son!
For the sake of attaining all-knowledge, you should maintain right mindfulness toward him.

Having thus provided him with various kinds of joy and benefit, the reciter should give rise to a compassionate mind; perceiving clearly that he is fit to be a disciple, he should thoroughly and skillfully instruct him.

When constantly reciting, one should perform the rite at a place where the various mountains are endowed with flowers and fruits, by the banks of pure and pleasing ponds or rivers praised by all Buddhas; or within a monastery, or in an araṇya, or among mountain springs; or in a secluded and remote place with a pure bathing site, free from obstacles and free from the clamor of sounds; or in whatever place the mind finds delight—at such a location, one should perform the recitation.
"Whenever a practitioner of yoga first rises from sleep, they should immediately form the Great Seal for Awakening All Buddhas and recite this mantra: 'Oṃ vajra tiṣṭha.

As for the seal: with the two hands of śamatha and vipaśyanā, each forms a vajra-fist; the two thumbs (tarjanī) are hooked together, the two index fingers (madhyamā) are held upright and pressed against each other like a needle, and the seal is placed upon one's heart."

Recite the preceding secret mantra three times—this is the recitation of all Buddhas—and awaken from samādhi. One should observe that all phenomena are like reflections, and then contemplate the meaning of this verse:
"All phenomena are like reflections, Pure and free from turbidity or defilement;
Without grasping and beyond description, They arise through the power of karma."
"Having thus realized this dharma, which is devoid of intrinsic nature and without support, one benefits immeasurable sentient beings; this is the mind-born of the Tathāgata.
Then, rising from his seat and wishing to depart, he immediately recited these secret words:
"Vajra-vīka. If one is staying in a dwelling, one should recite this secret mantra:
"Tiṣṭha vajra. If one wishes to converse with others, one should visualize the syllable *raṃ* upon the tongue and recite this secret mantra:
"Raṃ vajrapāśa. When washing the face, one recites this secret mantra, saying:

"Oṃ vajra-rāga-lāgye kiliṃ jaḥ svāhā vajra-tuṣya huḥ. With each recitation of this mantra, one should immediately wash one's face with water; doing so seven times, reciting it seven times, one will then obtain the gaze of all Tathāgatas.
"If there are any Māras or others who are violent and malevolent, they will all feel joy toward this person; furthermore, one may empower water seven times with secret mantras and use it."

"When one wishes to chew a tooth-stick, one should first recite the secret mantra of the Vajra-Laughter of all Tathāgatas seven times before chewing it; this can destroy all afflictions and secondary afflictions."
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ vajrahasa hā. Having formed the mudrā by visualizing the two wings as a vajra-fist, one chews it.
"If you wish to relieve yourself, first adorn your body with the Armor Mudrā (*kavaca-mudrā*) and recite this secret mantra:

*Oṃ chinda*. Protecting yourself with this secret mantra, perform the ritual of the mudrā as follows: form the Vajra-fists with both hands of *śamatha* (calm abiding) and *vipaśyanā* (insight). Extend the fingers of the *vīrya-bala* (effort-power) and visualize the syllable *Oṃ* at the tip of the *vīrya-bala* finger. Visualize the syllable *Chinda* at the tip of the *prajñā-bala* (wisdom-power) finger. Upon the heart, bind the *vīrya-bala* fingers and encircle them three times like the fastening of armor. Then move it to the back, then to the navel and waist; circle the knees, the throat, and the neck; push it forward from the forehead and backward behind the neck, circling each three times like the fastening of armor. Finally, let it hang down and gradually release it from the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *madhyamā* (middle finger), like a celestial robe, until it reaches the heart and stops there."
"When one wishes to perform purification, one should form the vajra-fist with the hand used for stopping [obstacles] and extend the thumb.
Having bound this mudrā and recited the syllable HŪṂ, one first takes up the ritual earth."

"Furthermore, those who practice recitation in pursuit of superior and virtuous goals are frequently obstructed by evil māras who constantly watch for their weak points. Whether in places of excrement and urine or in various defiled and impure locations, these beings cause harm; therefore, one should provide protection through secret mantras, mudrās, and so forth, so that they may find no opportunity."
"When about to enter the latrine, one should immediately visualize oneself as the syllable *laṃ*, with the syllables *hūṃ* visualized on the left and right.
One should further visualize one's body as vajra, possessing flaming fangs of fire."
Then recite the secret mantra:

Oṃ vajranara mahānutāśvavilocaya sarvabhūmi-kuru sarvanuṣṭhān hūṃ phaṭ. Regarding the ritual mudrā: form the wrathful Vajra-fist with the thumbs tucked inside; one should assume a wrathful expression with glaring eyes, knitted brows, and a fierce gaze. Placing it upon the crown of the head, the two shoulders, the heart, and the throat, all evils of the three realms will be eliminated.
Furthermore, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ kuru nairṛtye hūṃ phaṭ. This mantra and its mudrā protect the body in all places and enable one to remain far removed from all evils.
Next, having finished the business of the toilet and completed the ritual cleansing, one should form the mudrā and recite the secret mantra, rinsing the mouth well with *vajra*-water.
The secret mantra is:

*Oṃ vajranāgadhaṭa*. As for the mudrā: form the *vajra-muṣṭi* (vajra-fist) by joining the thumbs; extend the three fingers representing aspiration, skillful means, and wisdom. One should then rinse the mouth, and having finished rinsing, one should proceed to bathe.
"Now, there are four methods for bathing; one should practice them daily at will according to the Dharma:

first, abiding in the threefold restraint (trisaṃvara); second, confessing and making requests; third, making offerings with mantras; and fourth, bathing with water. These four methods should be practiced by the wise."
If entering into water, one should visualize the Lake of the Joyful Gods (*Tuṣita*). Within that lake, one should visualize the Tathāgata family with the syllable *vaṃ*;
the Vajra family with the syllable *hūṃ*;
and the Ratna family with the syllable *traḥ*.
One should visualize the syllable *Hrīḥ* as the Lotus Family;
one should visualize the syllable *A* as the Karma Family.

Having done this, one further visualizes the deity of the secret mantra one is reciting residing in its respective family. Next, one visualizes the supreme maṇḍala-cakra of the Tathāgata within the water, and contemplates the five families upon that maṇḍala-cakra. One then purifies that water by means of secret mantras, mudrās, and so forth.

When the bathing ritual is completed, one should cup pure scented water with both hands, recite the secret mantra one maintains over it, and offer it to all the Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and the original deities.
"Once the offerings have been made, one should visualize that wheel entirely entering into one's own body.

Having visualized this, one emerges from the water according to the ritual and stands upon the shore, adorning the body with the head-ornament and other mudrās. One holds the *vajra* of the flaming Garuḍa-Vajrapāṇi with the right hand, and holds the bell of the radiant Vajra of the left hand. One dons fine silken garments and celestial robes, holds a white *kakkola* nut in the mouth, and chews camphor so that the breath is fragrant."

With a concentrated mind, one should generate great compassion within that interval, remaining free from anger and free from attachment. Without looking upon impurities or any outcastes (*caṇḍāla*), one should visualize walking upon an eight-petaled lotus and the manifestation of offering implements of the three times. One should contemplate the supreme and vast offerings held by oneself through the visualization of the *vidyā*, and further reflect upon the profound principle of the true nature of the secret mantra held by oneself.

"One should proceed to the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). When about to enter, one should first recite the secret mantras according to the aforementioned method, wash the feet with water, and rinse the mouth. Having finished these acts, from the very moment they began, one should maintain the *vajramuṣṭi* (vajra-fist) seal without dispersing it, placing it upon the heart."

"At the time of opening the door, one should recite the secret mantra *HŪṂ* and, with wrathful eyes, dispel all obstacles. Thereafter, abiding in right mindfulness with a respectful mind, one should pay homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ten directions—those who have attained mastery over all phenomena and the supreme sphere of wisdom."

Having prostrated with the five limbs touching the ground, one next kneels on both knees and performs the confession of all transgressions, as well as the requests for teaching, the sympathetic rejoicing, the making of vows, and the dedication of merit; having spoken these according to one's capacity, one again prostrates.
Next, rising from his seat, he again placed his right knee upon the ground and immediately bound the Great Mudrā of Vajradhara, reciting this mantra: "Oṃ vajra muḥ.

As for the method of the mudrā: place the palms facing downward with the left hand below and the right hand above, with the backs joined and extended; then interlace the fingers of the *dhyāna* (left) and *prajñā* (right) hands, as well as the *dāna* (left thumb) and *jñāna* (right thumb), with one another.

By reciting this secret mantra and forming the great mudrā, one can cause all Buddhas to rejoice; one will immediately attain the merit of making offerings to, honoring, and prostrating before all Tathāgatas, Vajrasattvas, and the rest.

"Next, offer your own body before all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas; first, prostrate yourself fully on the ground toward the four directions with this sublime Dharma, joining your palms and extending your hands, performing one full prostration for each direction."
"First, in the eastern direction, recite this secret mantra and perform prostration:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pūjā-vasat-anayātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhiṣṭhasva saṃmukhībhava me hūṃ.*" The commentary states:
"In the Sanskrit original, the first and last words are preserved; the other directions follow this example."
In order to make offerings to and serve all Tathāgatas, I now offer my own body; may all Tathāgatas, as Vajrasattvas, grant me their protection.
"Furthermore, as before, join the vajra-palms at the heart and prostrate toward the south with the forehead to the ground, reciting the mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pūjā-viśeṣa-ātmanam niryātayāmi, adya me sarvatathāgata-vajraratna-viśodhaya abhiṣiñca māṃ tala tala*. The commentary states:
'In order to make an offering for the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of all Tathāgatas, I now offer my own body; may all Tathāgatas grant me the consecration of the Vajra-Jewel.'"
Furthermore, placing the vajra-pañjali at the crown of the head and touching the lips to the ground, one should prostrate toward the western direction and recite the mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākare pramardanaya jvala ātmanan niryātaya me sarvatathāgata-vajradharmadhara pravartaya māṃ hīḥ*. The commentary states:
"In order to successively make offerings to all the Tathāgatas, one offers up one's own body, vowing that all the Tathāgatas shall cause the Vajradharma wheel to turn for me."
Furthermore, with the vajra-pañjali joined, place it from the head down upon the heart; bowing with the crown of the head toward the north, recite this mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatabhuja-karmani adhaman niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrakarma kuru me 'rthaṃ svāhā*. The commentary states:
"In order to perform the activities for the worship of all Tathāgatas, one offers up one’s own body, vowing that all Tathāgatas shall perform vajra-activities for one."

"Having performed prostrations in the four directions according to the aforementioned method, one should next sit according to one's own direction, each performing the specific rites—such as the removal of calamities, augmentation, subjugation, or *abhicāra*—as desired."

"If one wishes to eliminate calamities, one should face north and sit in the *paryaṅka* posture—meaning sitting with the knees pressed together and the legs crossed—and clearly recite the secret mantra (*mantra*) with eyes of compassion, neither too hurried nor too slow, maintaining it with right mindfulness. As for 'eyes of compassion,' they are like Mount Sumeru and Mount Mandara, firm and unmoving; such unblinking eyes are called 'eyes of compassion. They can eliminate all malevolent spirits and various types of malarial fevers. Then he spoke the secret mantra:

"Oṃ nṛtya nṛtyeṣṭa ṭraṭṭa. If one is performing for the purpose of increase (*puṣṭi*), one should face the east, sit in the lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) with legs crossed, gaze with the *vajra-eye*, and then begin the recitation with *vajra-speech*. Regarding the *vajra-gaze*: it means looking with eyes full of affection and joy; by gazing in this way, all shall be brought into compliance. Then, he spoke these secret words:

"Oṃ vajra-nairṛtya-matha. If one wishes to subjugate [an opponent], one should face west and sit in the bhadrapīṭha posture, squatting with both feet together so that the buttocks do not touch the ground. One should then subjugate them by means of the 'fierce eye' (*tīkṣṇa-dṛṣṭi*). The fierce eye consists of twitching and repeatedly blinking the eyes. All who are looked upon with this eye shall be subjugated. Then, the secret mantra is recited:"

"Oṃ nairṛtyāyakuśiṅga. If performing an *abhicāra* rite, one should face south, stand upright with the right foot planted in the *pratyālīḍha* posture, and extend the left leg like the letter "T" of the world; the body is bent and leaning slightly. Alternatively, one may sit in the *utkuṭaka* posture, placing the right foot upon the left, with the buttocks not touching the ground. One should fix a wrathful gaze, raising the eyebrows and squinting the eyes.
By gazing in this manner, all malevolent spirits and ghosts shall be utterly destroyed. Reciting with a wrathful mind and angry eyes, one utters the secret mantra:
"Oṃ krodhanetriṣi hūṃ phaṭ. Generally, when reciting a secret mantra with a wrathful tone of voice, it is said that one should pronounce the syllable *hūṃ* like a cloud-shading sound;
when reciting a subjugating mantra with a wrathful voice, one adds the two syllables *hūṃ* and *phaṭ*, both of which must have their sounds and meanings clearly articulated.
Regarding the recitation of the secret mantra, it is like the syllable *pha*: one assumes an expression of wrath, with a countenance clearly manifesting fierce anger, and recites it.

Whether one performs the full *paryaṅka* (cross-legged) posture of the Tathāgata or the half-*paryaṅka* (half-lotus) posture of the Great Bodhisattvas, it is for the sake of purifying all sentient beings.
One who seeks to dwell in purity while abiding in right mindfulness should recite this mantra with the mind focused on its meaning:
*Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’ham* (Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by their very nature; I too am pure by my very nature). The commentary states:
The word *brahma* (purity) is preserved in the initial syllable (*oṃ*). Since all phenomena are pure by their very nature, I too am pure by my very nature.
"Having recited this secret mantra, one should further contemplate in the mind:
'These sentient beings have wandered through birth and death since beginningless time; obscured by the dark gloom of the defilements of stinginess and greed, their eyes remain unopened.'"
"In order to eliminate the obstacles of stinginess and greed, and to bring about the accomplishment of all mundane and supramundane *siddhis*.
Having completed this reflection, he then recited this secret mantra: "Oṃ sarvatathāgata-saṃsiddha-sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasiddhyai svabhāva-tathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-dharme. The Commentary states:
The syllable *Bram* (Vaṃ) is the first letter, praised by all Tathāgatas; it ensures that for all sentient beings, all *siddhis* and aspirations shall be fully accomplished.
"Whatever obstacles arise, they all originate from the mind, due to the power of habitual stinginess and greed accumulated in the past."
"In order to eliminate and extinguish obstacles, one should recollect the bodhicitta.

Having reflected thus for a brief moment, the practitioner of yoga should observe that the world is gripped by violence, fear, and false conceptualization; that its mental activities are deluded by craving and longing; that it is consumed by the fire of hatred; that its body constantly wanders in the darkness of ignorance; that its mind is submerged in the mud of passionate attachment; that it is perpetually intoxicated by the wine of false pride and arrogance; and that it dwells within the house of birth and death characterized by wrong views, failing to encounter the supreme nectar of the spiritual friend—all due to the infinite varieties produced by the craftsmanship of its own various false conceptualizations.
“Seeing that all sentient beings are shrouded by the heavy defilement of ignorance, and seeing such faults as these for which they have no refuge or protection, one should feel compassion for them.
Having given rise to a heart of compassion, one acts for the sake of delivering immeasurable sentient beings.”
"If the practitioner who maintains the recitation wishes to enter meditative absorption (*samādhi*), they should first manifest the *āpophanaga* (or *apophana*) samādhi.

Next, the method for entering samādhi is explained: 'One who desires to enter concentration must not move the body or any of its limbs; the lips and teeth should be joined, and the two eyes should appear as if closed. Before the image of the Buddha, one should first contemplate the intention to enter concentration, reflecting thus:
"The Buddhas pervade space, just as the earth is saturated with the oiliness of sesame seeds; likewise, they are arrayed within my own body and mind."'"

Having formed this thought, he immediately binds the *samaya* and other mudrās. He then visualizes the syllable *HŪṂ* upon his own tongue, heart, body, and hands, and visualizes that these syllables transform into vajras.

Furthermore, he visualizes the syllable *MA* in his right eye and the semi-vowel *ṬA* (pronounced as a half-syllable) in his left eye; he then visualizes the syllable *MA* transforming into the moon and the syllable *ṬA* transforming into the sun. With eyes thus formed of vajra, he should gaze upon all Buddhas. By gazing in this manner, one obtains the praise of all Buddhas.
Recite this secret mantra:

"Oṃ vajramatha. Having thus performed the gazing with the Vajra-eye as previously described and completed this recitation of the secret mantra, all those who should be subdued will constantly comply. Furthermore, through the gaze of the Vajra-dharma, any violent or evil beings, as well as all obstructing *vināyakas*, shall be utterly destroyed.

"Next, perform the ritual for binding the samaya-mudrā; once the wings of śamatha and vipaśyanā have been made firm, interlace the initial portions of all the pāramitās—this is called the 'Vajra-joined palms' (vajra-añjali)."

Placing it upon the crown, with the two palms at the heart and throat according to their respective positions, one recites the mantra for the sake of empowering one’s own body and places them in sequence.
The mantra is: *Oṃ vajra-jvali*.

Furthermore, having formed the Vajra-joined palms mudrā (*vajra-añjali*)—which represents the culmination of all perfections—and having firmly locked the backs together, it is called the Vajra-bond mudrā (*vajra-bandha*).
Again, place the mudrā upon the heart and recite this secret mantra:

*vajra-bandhaya*. Furthermore, having formed the Vajrabandha-mudrā, extend the two fingers of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* families to form a needle, place it upon the heart, and immediately recite the secret mantra:
*samayasattva*. This is the secret mantra and mudrā for awakening all Buddhas and their disciples.

Next, take the mudrā-pins and bend them into the palms; with the *jñāna*, *samādhi*, *dāna*, and *prajñā* fingers held upright like needles, this is called the *Sukhāvatī-samaya-mudrā*. Then recite the mantra:

"Samaya-rakṣa. Furthermore, having formed the *vajra-bandha*, place it upon the heart and visualize the syllable *tra* upon one's own heart, with the syllable *ṭa* serving as the gateway to the heart.

When drawing the *vajra-bandha* mudrā, one should visualize it as opening the gate of wisdom; then, recite the mantra three times and draw [the mudrā] three times. The mantra is: *Oṃ vajrabandha kaṭaṭa*.

Having opened the gate of wisdom within the heart, one should then visualize a great palace inside that gate. Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *A* before oneself, radiating light everywhere. Because this serves to generate the bodhicitta and perfect great wisdom, one causes [the deity] to enter the palace of one’s own heart; then, with a mind of right concentration, one binds the *vajra-āvāhana-mudrā* and the *samaya-mudrā* to summon [the deity] in.

Regarding the ritual method for binding and summoning: having bound the vajra-bond mudrā, bend the two wisdom-fingers (index fingers) and insert them into the palms; this is called the Vajra-summoning-and-entering mudrā.
At the time of forming the bond, one recites the secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajra veśaya āḥ. Through this practice of yoga, the practitioner immediately attains the vajra-summoning wisdom.

This wisdom is able to comprehend all deeds performed in the past, future, and present; it fully awakens to and understands hundreds of thousands of kinds of sūtras never heard before, such that their words and meanings all manifest before one.

"Next, following the above procedure, having again formed the Vajravāṅ mudrā, bend the two wisdom and concentration fingers into the palms; place the two effort fingers upon the backs of the wisdom and concentration fingers. This is called the Vajramuṣṭi Samaya-mudrā."
When forming this seal, recite this secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajramuṣṭi vaṃ. As previously described, regarding the placement of the syllable *a* within the heart, one should constantly close the gates of the heart-palace with the syllable *vaṃ*.
This secret mantra is called the Vajra Fist Mudrā because it is able to grasp and maintain the vajra body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Having completed the explanation of this mudrā, one then places the *śamatha* (lower) fingers upon the *vipaśyanā* (upper) fingers, hooks the thumbs and wisdom fingers together, and extends the effort fingers upright to form the appearance of a roar; this is called the Mudrā of Decisive Victory through the Power of the Three Realms, and is also called the Great Power Mudrā.

To bind this seal (*mudrā*), one should first recite the syllable *HŪṂ* three times to form it, resembling the sound of thunder amidst dark clouds. Taking the final syllable of the secret mantra, one recites a single *HŪṂ PHAṬ*, and then utters this secret mantra:

*Oṃ sumbhanisumbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ.* This seal is rotated three times clockwise above the head. If there are any māras who create obstacles, upon seeing this seal they will all depart, and one further attains protection for one’s own body in all places.
Furthermore, by touching lamps, incense, flowers, food, drink, and so forth with this mudrā while reciting the syllable *HŪṂ* for each one, they become purified as soon as they are touched.
"Furthermore, having firmly bound the vajra-bond, join the two thumbs and the two little fingers together and extend them upright like needles; this is called the Vajrapadma Samaya-mudrā."
When forming this seal, recite the secret mantra:

*Oṃ vajrapadma samayasattva vaṃ*. By placing this seal upon the mouth while reciting the mantra, one becomes supreme within the Padmakula. Next, further observe with the most excellent wisdom that both the internal and external are entirely non-existent, and again contemplate that the three periods of time are equal to empty space.
Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *YAM* as the black realm of the earth-wind mandala;
then, one should visualize the syllable *KHAṂ* as the encircling mountain range, adorned with supreme jewels.

Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *vaṃ* in the sky; as the Buddha Vairocana, out of his compassion, causes milk to flow from both sides, the Cakravāḍa mountains then become a great ocean of nectar.
"Furthermore, within that ocean, one should visualize the syllable *praṃ* as the form of a tortoise; this tortoise is like gold in color, and its body is immeasurable yojanas in extent."
Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable *khriḥ* upon the back of the tortoise; this syllable transforms into a crimson color with crimson light.
The lotus is pleasing and exquisite, with three tiers, each having eight petals, complete with a central platform and filaments.
Upon that pedestal, one should visualize the three syllables *Bhraṃ*, *Hūṃ*, and *Khaṃ* as Mount Sumeru; this mountain is composed of various jewels and has eight corners.
"On the summit of the mountain, one should further visualize the five syllables—VAṂ, HŪṂ, TRA, KHRI, and AḤ (pronounced with emphasis)—as the great palace."

The palace was perfectly symmetrical at its four corners and possessed four gates; on the left and right of each gate stood auspicious banners, and it was surrounded by railings and four tiers of stairways.
Upon that palace are five multi-storied pavilions, adorned with various silk banners, pearl nets, and flower garlands suspended from them.

One should visualize that the four corners outside the palace and the corners of the gates are embellished with vajra-jewels; furthermore, the outer courtyard is further adorned with various bells made of diverse jewels that outshine the sun and moon, with hanging strings of pearls serving as ornaments, and beyond that, rows of immeasurable kalpa-trees.
Furthermore, one should visualize the exquisite voices and songs of the various devas, and the musical performances of the asuras and mahoraga kings, who delight themselves with vajra-dances.
Within that palace is a maṇḍala, adorned in its center by eight vajra-pillars.

Within the wheel of the Tathāgata family, one should visualize three seed-syllables: visualize the syllable *hṛdaya* (heart) in the center, and to its left and right, visualize the two long vowels *āḥ*. Through these three syllables, one accomplishes the subtle, four-faced, and square lion-throne of the deity.

Furthermore, within the Vajra family, one should visualize the seed-syllable *E*—the second of the three syllables—with the syllable *Hūṃ* visualized on its left and right; and with the Vajra family formed by these three seed-syllables, one takes an elephant as the seat.

Furthermore, within the Ratna family, one should visualize three seed-syllables: in the center, visualize the syllable *maṃ* with a heavy vowel; on the left and right, visualize the syllable *tra*. Within this Ratna family formed by these three seed-syllables, take a horse as the seat.

Furthermore, the Lotus Family has three seed-syllables: one should visualize the syllable *maṃ* at the center, and the syllable *hrīḥ* on the left and right. Within this Lotus Family formed by these three seed-syllables, a peacock serves as the seat.

Furthermore, within the Karma-kula there are three seed-syllables: one should visualize the syllable Khaḍga at the center, and the short syllable A on both the left and right. Within this Karma-kula formed by these three seed-syllables, one should visualize a garuḍa as the seat.

"Once one has visualized the seats of the aforementioned assemblies as described above, next visualize all the Tathāgatas, the sixteen great Bodhisattvas, and the four Pāramitās; then arrange the four kinds of internal offerings and the four kinds of external offerings, and furthermore, station the four Bodhisattvas who guard the four gates according to their respective directions."

Furthermore, as previously described, the various Buddhas, great Bodhisattvas, gatekeeping Bodhisattvas, and so forth, each by means of their own fundamental samādhi, and each from their own mind according to the characteristics of the seals and signs recorded for them as described below, should all be visualized as emerging from the body of Vairocana Buddha.

"Furthermore, one should visualize Vairocana Buddha in the four directions, seated upon those lion thrones of all Tathāgatas as described above, with bodies sustained by the reality of all Tathāgatas."

“Vairocana has manifested the attainment of perfect enlightenment since time immemorial; all Tathāgatas take Samantabhadra as their heart-mind. Furthermore, they employ the great maṇi-jewel produced from the space of all Tathāgatas for consecration, and they further attain the ultimate perfection of the Dharma-wisdom of Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas.”
Furthermore, when all Tathāgatas have completed their activities through the unobstructed commands of Viśvakarman and all that was sought has been fulfilled:

"Visualize Akṣobhya Buddha seated upon the elephant throne described above in the eastern direction; visualize Ratnasaṃbhava Buddha seated upon the horse throne described above in the southern direction; visualize Amitābha Buddha seated upon the peacock throne described above in the western direction; and visualize Amoghasiddhi Buddha seated upon the garuḍa throne described above in the northern direction."
On each seat, one should further visualize the form of a full moon, and upon that, visualize a lotus throne; on each and every lotus throne, a Buddha is seated therein.

At that time, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, taking the bodies of all Tathāgatas as his own essence, entered the samādhi called the Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna, which encompasses the names of all sentient beings and is born from the samaya of Samantabhadra Mahābodhisattva.
Having entered, this heart of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, emerged from his own heart and spoke these secret words: “Vajrasattva.

As soon as these secret words were spoken, from the heart of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One—he emerged as Samantabhadra in the form of a moon disc. Having purified the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings, he came to reside in the quarters of all the Tathāgatas.
From within those lunar discs, the vajra-wisdom of all Tathāgatas emerged and entered the heart of the Tathāgata Vairocana, because of his being Samantabhadra and because of his firmness.

From within the *vajrasattva-samādhi*, by means of the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas acting as a single secret essence, it pervades the extent of the realm of empty space, fully endowed with radiance as its five crowns.

Having thus accomplished the five-pronged vajra formed from the vajra body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, it emerged again from the hearts of all Tathāgatas and was placed within the right palm.
"At that time, furthermore, various colors and forms emerge from the vajra, and its radiant light shines forth, pervading all worlds.
One should further imagine that upon the peaks of these rays of light, Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds appear."

Once manifested, they pervade the entire Dharma-realm, filling the void of space and circulating throughout all worlds like clouds upon the ocean. They manifest the perfect enlightenment through the supernatural power of the Wisdom of Equality of all Tathāgatas; they can cause [beings] to generate the Great Bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas and achieve the various aspects of Samantabhadra’s conduct. They can also serve the retinues of all Tathāgatas, lead [beings] toward the site of Great Enlightenment, and further subdue all Māras. They enable the realization of the equality of all things, the attainment of Great Enlightenment, the turning of the True Wheel of Dharma, and even the protection of all sentient beings in all worlds, achieving the supreme siddhi of the supernatural wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

Having manifested the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of Samantabhadra and furthermore for the sake of the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they became a single secret essence and formed the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; then, abiding within the heart of Vairocana Buddha, they uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am Samantabhadra, the firm and steadfast sattva. Although I do not possess a physical form, I manifest spontaneously;
through my unshakable stability, I constitute the body of the sattva."
At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, having emerged from the heart of the Buddha, again requested instruction before all the Tathāgatas, relying upon a lunar disc.
At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Wisdom-Samaya of All Tathāgatas;
having manifested the wisdom, liberation, knowledge, and vision of the Khura Samādhi of all Tathāgatas,
he turned the wheel of the true Dharma, successively benefiting sentient beings through the power of great skillful means and diligence.
The Great Wisdom Samaya, which pervades the entire realm of sentient beings and protects them all,
acts as the sovereign lord for the sake of the enjoyment of all peace, happiness, and mental delight;
it is the supreme accomplishment of the fruit of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya, the supernatural powers of the equality-wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Because of this *siddhi*, all Tathāgatas, by means of this *siddhi-vajra*,
establish him in the rank of a universal wheel-turner (*cakravartin*) for the sake of that Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; therefore,
they consecrate him with the jewel-crown and silken streamers of the bodies of all Tathāgatas.
Having performed the consecration, he bestowed [the name] upon him.
At that time, because the Tathāgatas had conferred the consecration with the name Vajradhara, he was thereafter called Vajradhara.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi bent his left arm, manifesting the form of a fierce and powerful warrior; with his right hand, he grasped a *vajra*, brandishing and tossing it outward, and spoke these words in a loud voice:
"This *vajra* is the supreme *siddhi* of all Tathāgatas."
"I am Vajra; grant me your hand. With my vajra, I shall grasp the vajra.
This is the first [instruction] on the Bodhicitta-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the Samādhi of Vajrasattva.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, and having given rise to the empowerment of the Sattvavajra-samādhi, he issued from his own heart an invocation of the samayas of all Tathāgatas, named "The Heart of All Tathāgatas.
He then spoke this mantra: Vajra-rāga. As soon as these secret words were spoken, within the hearts of all Tathāgatas—namely, that Bodhisattva Vajradhara—he became the great hook of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, he immediately dwelt within the palm of the World-Honored One Vairocana.
At that time, from the body of that Great Hook, there appeared Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Once he has appeared, having performed the summoning and invitation of all Tathāgatas and so forth, as well as all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas, through the power of Amogharāja and the firmness of Vajrasattva, they merge into one to become the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja.
Having accomplished this, he dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and cried out in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
“I am Amogharāja, born from that Vajra,
acting as the great summoner.
Because of the accomplishment of all Buddhas, I can pervade all places and summon all Tathāgatas.”
Then, having emerged from the heart of the Buddha, that Bodhisattva Amogharāja took his place upon a moon disc to the right of all the Tathāgatas and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the samādhi of the Vajra-Samaya of Hook-Summoning of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of summoning all beings throughout the entire realm of sentient beings via the Samaya of Hook-Summoning of All Tathāgatas; and for the sake of providing all Tathāgatas with every comfort, delight, and enjoyment; and even for the sake of attaining the supreme siddhi and accomplishment sustained by the wisdom of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas—thereupon bestowed it upon the hands of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas conferred empowerment upon him by means of the name "Vajrākarṣaṇa" (Vajra Summoner).
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrākarṣaṇa, having summoned all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-hook, proclaimed aloud:
"I am the Tathāgatas, The unsurpassed vajra-wisdom."
"Capable of accomplishing the Buddha-works, the supreme summoner.
This is the second [chapter], the Wisdom of the Summoning of All Tathāgatas, the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *samaya* of the Great Bodhisattva Māra, and having arisen from the *sattvavajra-samādhi* through empowerment, he brought forth from his own body the *samaya* of the service of all Tathāgatas, named "The Heart of All Tathāgatas. He then spoke these secret words:
*vajra-rāga*. As soon as this mantra was spoken, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas—that is, from that World-Honored One Vajradhara—there emerged the flower implements of all the Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, they entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, as a single secret essence.
Thereupon, they remained within his palm in the form of vajra bows and arrows.

Having thus emerged from the bodies of all Tathāgatas, which were as numerous as the atoms in all worlds and identical to that body of the Vajra-Arrow, he performed services for all Tathāgatas and manifested all the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas.

Having performed this, because it constitutes the ultimate act of slaying and because the Vajrasattva samādhi is supremely firm, they merge into a single, secret union to form the body of the Mahābodhisattva Māra; having thus become so, he immediately dwells within the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Having settled there, he raised his voice and uttered these words:
"How marvelous! He said:
"My own nature is pure, yet through the affairs of passionate attachment,
I serve the Tathāgata.
Because it is free from defilement yet pure, and because it is stained, it is able to subdue."

At that time, the body of that great Bodhisattva Māra descended from the heart of Vairocana Buddha and, having taken his place within a moon disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas, again requested instruction.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra Empowerment of the Service of Passion for All Tathāgatas.

Having entered this meditative absorption, the *samaya* of the *mālana-vajra* of all Tathāgatas pervaded the entire realm of sentient beings. For the sake of bestowing all delightful enjoyments of peace and happiness, and even for the attainment of the supreme *siddhi* of the *māra-karma* of all Tathāgatas, he conferred that Vajra-Arrow upon the Great Bodhisattva Māra with both hands as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the name Vajracāpa and consecrated him with the title Vajracāpa.
Then, when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracāpa struck all the Tathāgatas with his vajra-arrows, he proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"These are all the Buddhas, The stainless wisdom free from attachment and defilement."
"By harming those who are defiled, one becomes free from defilement and all experience peace and happiness.
This is the third [section], the wisdom for serving all Tathāgatas, which is the samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Vajracāpa.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra-samādhi of the Sattva-blessing born from the samaya of the Great Sattva Rājavikrīḍita. From his own body and mind, he brought forth the joy of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and then uttered this secret mantra:

*Vajrasādhu*. As soon as this mantra was spoken, from the heart of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Vajradhara—there arose the thought of "Excellent" (*sādhu*) toward all Tathāgatas; they then merged into one and entered the heart of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Once it had entered the heart, it became the essence of Vajra-Ānanda and dwelt within the palms of both hands.
At that time, from that essence of Vajra-Ānanda, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.
Once he had appeared, he performed the "Excellent! (*sādhu*) and other deeds for all the Tathāgatas.

Having performed the miraculous transformations of all the Tathāgatas, because of his extreme joy and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* was exceedingly firm, he merged completely with them and became the body of the Mahāsattva Saṃtoṣaṇarāja. Abiding within the heart of the Tathāgata Vairocana, he proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! (*aho*)"
He said: “‘I am the most supreme, the All-Knowing One, as is universally proclaimed.
If one eliminates all false imaginings and conceptual discriminations, they will always rejoice upon hearing [this].’”
At that time, the Mahāsattva King Joy descended from the heart of the Buddha and dwelt within a moon-disc behind the backs of all the Tathāgatas, again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra of Joy of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of providing all joy, peace, and delightful enjoyment to the entire realm of sentient beings through the *samaya* of the supreme, ultimate joy-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and even for the sake of attaining the fruit of the *siddhi* of the most excellent flavor through the supreme exultation of all Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajra of Rapture upon the hands of that King of Joy, Mahābodhisattva, as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajra-ullāsa and consecrated him with that vajra-name.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajra-ullāsa, having caused all the Buddhas to rejoice with the sound of "Excellent! (sādhu) by means of the vajra-sign of joy, spoke these words aloud:
"This is the turning [of the wheel] by the Buddhas; Excellent is the one who is able to turn it."
"This sublime vajra is able to increase joy.
This is the fourth, the Wisdom of "Excellent" (Sādhu) enacted by all Tathāgatas, the Samaya of the Vajra-Leap Mahāsattva.
"These four bodhisattvas are all members of the retinue of Akṣobhya Buddha within the Vajra Family; they are collectively titled Sarvatathāgata-mahāsamayasattva."

Then, the Blessed One again emerged from the heart of Ākāśagarbha into the Mahābodhisattva-samaya-born Ratnādhiṣṭhānavajra-samādhi; this Samaya of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, issued forth from his own heart, and he spoke these secret words:

"Vajra-āratna. As soon as this mantra was uttered, it filled the entirety of space from the hearts of all Tathāgatas. Because of the perfect discernment of the Wisdom of Equality (*samatājñāna*), and because of the firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single unity. That very Vajradhara then emitted light that pervaded the entirety of space; because that light which pervaded the entirety of space shone forth, the "entirety" was taken as the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*).
At that time, through the power of the empowerment of all Buddhas, the entire realm of empty space entered the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana.

Because he had practiced it well, the *vajrasattva-samādhi* became the universal treasury of empty space, circulating throughout all worlds; a body formed from great *vajra*-jewels, equal in measure [to that treasury], came to abide within the palms of the Tathāgata.
At that time, having emerged from that great adamantine jewel body in numbers equal to the atoms of all worlds, they performed all the rites such as the consecration of all Tathāgatas.

After all the Tathāgatas have performed their miraculous transformations throughout all worlds, because they have perfectly brought forth the treasury of the entire world-system and because the Vajrasattva samādhi is utterly firm, they merge into one as a single secret union and accomplish the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Once it was accomplished, he dwelt in the mind of Vairocana and uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
"I am the self-consecrated, the unsurpassed Vajraratna;
though I have no dwelling or attachment, I am nevertheless the Lord of the Three Realms."
Then, that Ākāśagarbha Mahābodhisattva descended from the heart of Vairocana Buddha, proceeded before all the Tathāgatas, and, relying upon a moon disc, again requested instruction.

“At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Great Maṇi-jewel Vajra Samādhi, whereby all that the Tathāgatas desire and seek is brought to fulfillment. This samaya pervades the entire realm of sentient beings for the sake of attaining all benefits, for the sake of all peace, happiness, and delightful enjoyments, and even for the sake of attaining the supreme siddhi of accomplishing the activities of all Tathāgatas; thus, this Vajra-maṇi became that Ākāśagarbha Mahābodhisattva.”
Because he was to turn the wheel of the vajra-jewel, he was further consecrated with the empowerment of the vajra-jewel treasury.
Having been consecrated, [the Buddhas] bestowed it upon him with both hands.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the name Vajragarbha as his empowerment title.
At that time, the Mahābodhisattva Vajragarbha, having placed that vajra-maṇi upon his own site of consecration, spoke these words in a loud voice:
"These Tathāgatas have granted permission; It can consecrate the crowns of sentient beings."
"I am the one who bestows by hand, as well as the one to whom it is bestowed;
with jewels, I adorn jewels.
This is the first Jewel-Wisdom Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, belonging to the Vajragarbha Mahābodhisattva of the Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata Family.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the jewel empowerment born from the *samaya* of the Mahāsattva of Great Majestic Light. From within himself, he brought forth the *samaya* of the light of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and uttered this secret mantra from his own heart:

“Vajra dīrgha. As soon as this secret mantra was uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he became a great sun-disk. Merging into a single unity, he entered the heart of Vairocana Buddha and immediately became the body of the Vajra-Sun, abiding within the palms of the Tathāgata.
At that time, from within the body of that Vajrasūrya, there emerged Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.
Having emerged, they performed such deeds as emitting the light of all Tathāgatas.

After all the Tathāgatas had performed their miraculous transformations, by means of their supreme and great majestic light, they accomplished the body of the Vajrasattva-samādhi Mahābodhisattva; abiding within the heart of Vairocana, they cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: “Possessing incomparable and great majestic radiance, he is able to illumine the realms of sentient beings;
causing all Buddhas to rely upon and protect him, though he is already pure, he remains thus.”
"Within purity, one can further purify.

At that time, the body of the Mahābodhisattva Vimalatejaprabha descended from the heart of the Buddha and took his place within a moon disc to the right of the Tathāgata, whereupon he again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the *vajra-samādhi* empowered by the circular light of all Tathāgatas, manifested an incomparable majestic radiance throughout the entire realm of sentient beings through the *samaya* of the light of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of providing the enjoyment of peace, happiness, and joy to all, and for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of the *siddhi* of the light of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, he took that Vajrasūrya and bestowed it upon the hands of that Mahābodhisattva Mahātejaḥprabha.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas collectively conferred upon him the name Vajraprabha and consecrated him with the Vajra-name.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrāvabhāsa, having illuminated all the Tathāgatas with his Vajra-sun, proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the wisdom of all Buddhas, Which eradicates the darkness of ignorance."
"By a measure equal to a mote of dust, it surpasses the light of the sun.
This is the second [samādhi], the Wisdom of the Circular Halo of All Tathāgatas, belonging to the Great Bodhisattva Vajraprabha.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra-samādhi of Jewel-Sustenance Born from the Samaya of Bodhisattva Ratnaketu. Having been able to fulfill the samayas sought by all Tathāgatas, that which is named the Heart of All Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart, and he then spoke these secret words:

“Vajra-kiṭu. As soon as these secret words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there appeared a jewel-banner (*ratnaketu*) adorned with various exquisite and multicolored ornaments.
Having emerged, they merge together as one and enter the heart of Vairocana, whereby they become the body of the Vajradhvaja.
Once accomplished, they abide within the palm of the Buddha’s hand.
At that time, from within the body of Vajradhvaja, there emerged Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.
Having emerged, they established all the activities of the precious banners of the Tathāgatas.

Having performed all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas, by virtue of the Great Jewel Banner and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into one as a single body of Mahābodhisattva. He then dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana and uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "The peerless Banner of Measurelessness, I am able to bestow it upon you;
all benefits and the fulfillment of *siddhi*."
"Whatever is sought, all shall be fulfilled.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnaketu, having descended from the heart of the Buddha, took his place within a moon disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the empowerment established by all Tathāgatas, was able to establish the *samaya* of the *cintāmaṇi-dhvaja* (jewel-banner) contemplation of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of exhausting the entire realm of sentient beings, for the sake of fulfilling all aspirations, all peace, and all pleasant enjoyments, and even for the sake of attaining the fruit of the supreme *siddhi* of the great benefit of all Tathāgatas, he placed that jewel-banner as described above into the palms of both hands.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas designated him by the name Vajraketu and consecrated him with the vajra-name.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraketu, by means of that vajra-banner, caused all the Tathāgatas to be in accord with the dānapāramitā, and proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
“This is for all the Tathāgatas, Who seek to bring [the perfections] to fulfillment.”
"It is named 'Wish-Fulfilling Banner,' the gateway to the *dānapāramitā*.
This is the third [chapter], the wisdom of the *dānapāramitā* of all Tathāgatas, belonging to the samādhi of Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajra-samādhi* called "The Jewel Empowerment Born from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva Constantly Loving and Joyful Roots. From his own body and mind, he brought forth this "Love-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:

*Vajra hā va*. As soon as these secret words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he manifested as the smile of all Tathāgatas. Unifying in a single secret union, he entered the heart of Vairocana Tathāgata and became the body of the Vajra Smile, abiding within the palms of the Tathāgata.
“At that time, from that body of vajra-smile, there appeared Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, and all the rare and wondrous deeds of the Tathāgatas.”

Having performed the miraculous displays and playful manifestations of all Tathāgatas, because his faculty of constant love and joy is so firm and because the Vajrasattva-samādhi is extremely stable, he becomes the body of a Great Bodhisattva.
Having thus achieved accomplishment and abiding within the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana, he uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
“I am the Great Laughter, supreme among all victors;
ever abiding securely in meditative concentration, I perform the work of a Buddha.”
At that time, the Mahābodhisattva Nityapramuditendriya descended from the heart of the Buddha and remained within a moon-disc behind all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the rare empowerment of all Tathāgatas, manifested the *samaya* of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of sentient beings. For the sake of providing the unsurpassed enjoyment of peace and joy for all faculties, and ultimately to attain the fruit of the supernatural powers and the wisdom of purifying the faculties of all Tathāgatas, he placed that *vajra-smile* into the palms of both hands of the Mahābodhisattva Nityapriyānandendriya, as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajrarāga and conferred upon him the consecration by means of that vajra-name.
Then, the Mahābodhisattva Vajrarāga, with a vajra-smile, smiled at all the Tathāgatas and proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the manifestation of birth by all the Tathāgatas, Displaying what is rare and marvelous."
"The Great Wisdom leaps forth, something unknown to those of the Two Vehicles.
This is the fourth, the rare wisdom of the smile of all Tathāgatas, [belonging to] the Vajraprema Mahābodhisattva.
“Thus, these four bodhisattvas within the Ratna family are the great consecrated *sattvas* of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the Vajra-samādhi empowered by the Dharma-samaya arising from the Mahābodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. From his own heart-mind, he brought forth the Dharma-samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and uttered this secret mantra:

“Vajra-dharma. As soon as this secret mantra was uttered, within the bodies of all Tathāgatas—that is, within that Bhagavān Vajradhara—there arose the light of the Dharma, because of his thorough realization of the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena through their intrinsic purity, and because of the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi.
From the radiance of those dharmas, all worlds appeared and were universally illuminated, thereby becoming the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).

At that time, that entire Dharma-realm filled the realm of empty space (*ākāśadhātu*), merging as one, and entered the heart of Vairocana Buddha. Pervading the extent of the realm of empty space, it became a great lotus-body and remained within the hands of the World-Honored One.
At that time, from within that Vajra-Lotus Body, the World-Honored One manifested bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having thus manifested, he performed the samādhi-wisdom, supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), and miraculous displays (*vikrīḍita*) of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds. Then, by virtue of the contemplation of Avalokiteśvara and the firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single unity to become the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having attained accomplishment, he dwelt within the heart of Vairocana Buddha and uttered these words with a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
“I am the ultimate truth, inherently pure from the beginning;
the raft is a metaphor for all dharmas, through which one can attain supreme purity.”
Then, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having descended from the heart of the Buddha, took his place within a moon-disc before all the Tathāgatas and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the Vajra Samādhi born from the Samaya of the Wisdom of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas, was able to purify the Samaya throughout the entire realm of sentient beings. For the sake of his own purification and for the enjoyment of the peace, bliss, and joy of all, and even unto the attainment of the fruit of the supernatural powers of the Dharma-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, he took that Great Vajra Lotus as described above and bestowed it upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara. For the purpose of turning the wheel of the true Dharma and for the consecration of the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas, he presented it with both hands.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas again conferred empowerment upon him with the name Vajranetra.
Then, because the petals of that lotus had blossomed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra was freed from the nature of craving and attachment, becoming pure and undefiled.
Having made this observation, he cried out these words in a loud voice:
"This is the wisdom of all Buddhas, Which can fully awaken one to craving and attachment;
Both I and those to whom I transmit it Abide in the Dharma through the Dharma."
"This is the first Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Vajranetra of the Lotus Family, the Observational Wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
From the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-saṃgraha-pāṭha-sūtra*, Fascicle One. (The title is repeated).

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Dharma Empowerment Born from the Samaya of Mañjuśrī Mahābodhisattva; then, from his own heart, he brought forth this Great Wisdom Samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:

"Vajratīkṣṇa. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he emerged as the Sword of Wisdom. He then merged into one and entered the heart of Buddha Vairocana, becoming the scabbard for the sword.
Once it was accomplished, it rested in the hand of Vairocana Buddha.

At that time, from within the sheath of that Tathāgata’s body, there emerged the bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to all worlds, the wisdoms of all Tathāgatas, and the miraculous displays of all Tathāgatas. Then, due to the supreme excellence of Mañjuśrī and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi, they merged into a single, inseparable unity to become the body of Mañjuśrī Mahābodhisattva.
Having thus achieved accomplishment, he went to the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
“I am the speech of all Buddhas, known by the name Mañjuśrīghoṣa;
though I have no form or color, my voice may be perceived.”

At that time, Mañjuśrī Mahābodhisattva, having descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place within a moon-disc on the right side of all the Tathāgatas and again requested instruction.

At that time, Vairocana Buddha, having entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra-Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, manifested the *samādhi* of the Severance of Afflictions of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of completely severing all suffering throughout the realm of sentient beings, for the sake of providing all forms of peace, joy, and enjoyment, and even for the sake of accomplishing the supreme *siddhi* of the Perfect Wisdom of the Conforming Voice of All Tathāgatas, he placed those vajras into the two hands of the Mahābodhisattva Mañjuśrī as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajrabodhi and conferred upon him the empowerment with the name Vajra.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrabodhi, having brandished and struck with his vajra-sword, cried out these words in a loud voice:
"This is the Prajñāpāramitā Of all the Tathāgatas."
"It can destroy all enemies and is supreme among those that extinguish sins.
This is the second, the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, belonging to the Vajrabodhi Mahābodhisattva Samādhi.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajra-samādhi* known as the "Dharma-Sustenance Born from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva Who Can Turn the Dharma-Wheel of All Tathāgatas upon the Mere Arising of the Thought. Immediately, from his own heart, he brought forth this *samaya* of the Dharma-wheel of all Tathāgatas, named the "Heart of All Tathāgatas," and spoke these secret words:

*Vajra-īdu*. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he emerged as the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm. Having emerged, they merged into one and entered the heart of the Buddha Vairocana, becoming the body of the Vajra Wheel, and remained within the hands of the Tathāgata.
At that time, from that Vajracakra-body, there emerged Tathāgata-bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, because they were able to turn the wheel of Dharma through the mere arousal of the thought of enlightenment (*cittotpāda*), and because the Vajrasattva-samādhi is exceedingly firm, they became the bodies that turn the wheel of Dharma through the mere arousal of the thought of enlightenment.
Having achieved this, he abides in the heart of Vairocana Buddha and proclaims these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He says:
"Among the Vajradharas, the Vajracakra is supreme;
by merely generating the thought [of awakening], he is able to turn the wheel of Dharma."

At that time, as soon as he had resolved his mind, the Mahābodhisattva Cakravartī descended from the heart of the Buddha and remained within the lunar disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas, whereupon he again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra-Eye Wheel of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of the *samaya* of the Great Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas—to cause all sentient beings throughout the realms of existence to enter the wheel of non-retrogression, to provide them with all peace, joy, and enjoyments, and ultimately to achieve the supreme *siddhi* of turning the wheel of the True Dharma for all Tathāgatas—he took that very vajra-wheel and conferred it upon the hands of the Mahābodhisattva Just-Generated-Mind-Turning-the-Wheel-of-Dharma, as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name "Vajramaṇḍala.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajramaṇḍala, having established the vajra-wheel for the sake of the non-retrogression of all the Tathāgatas, again proclaimed these words with a loud voice:
"This is the [wheel] of all the Tathāgatas, Which is able to purify and cleanse all things."
"This is called non-retrogression, the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) for the path to awakening.
This is the third wisdom of the Vajra-maṇḍa Mahābodhisattva, by which the mere arising of the thought of awakening can turn the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajrasamādhi* born from the dharma-sustenance of the *samaya* of the Silent Mahābodhisattva. Immediately, from his own heart, he brought forth the *samaya* of the recitation of all Tathāgatas, named "The Heart of All Tathāgatas," and spoke these secret words:

*Vajra-bhāṣa*. As soon as these words were uttered, they emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, as the dharma-syllables of all Tathāgatas—and having emerged, they merged into one and entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha. Thereupon, they became the body of Vajra-recitation and remained within the palms of the World-Honored One.
At that time, from the body of Vajra Recitation, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, they performed all the miraculous displays of the nature of the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas; then, because they were extremely firm and stable, they merged into a single, unified whole.
Having become the body of the Vajra-bodhisattva of Speech, he dwelt within the heart of Vairocana Buddha and spoke these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "The secret of nature, I speak as a secret language;
if one explains the True Dharma, one remains far removed from verbal proliferation."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avāca descended from the heart of the Buddha and remained within a moon-disc behind the backs of all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the *samaya* of the secret speech of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of accomplishing the *siddhi* of speech throughout the entire realm of sentient beings through the *samaya* of the wisdom of the speech of all Tathāgatas; for the sake of the enjoyment of all peace, bliss, and delight; and even for the sake of attaining the supreme *siddhi* of the secret nature of the speech of all Tathāgatas—he then bestowed those very vajra-recitations upon the hands of that Wordless Mahābodhisattva as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajrabhāṣa.
Then, having conversed with all the Tathāgatas through the vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*), the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrabhāṣa proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the vajra-recitation of all the Tathāgatas."
"Regarding the secrets of all Tathāgatas, one is able to achieve swift accomplishment.
This is the fourth [wisdom], the wisdom of all Tathāgatas free from verbal proliferation, the Samādhi of the Mahābodhisattva Vajravāc of the Lotus Family.
“The four bodhisattvas above are the Great Wisdom Samaya-sattvas of all Tathāgatas of the Lotus Family.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra Samādhi of the Karma-empowerment Born from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas. Immediately, from his own body and mind, he manifested the Karma-samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:”

“Vajra-karma. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there appeared the light of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, because he is perfectly proficient in the wisdom of equality regarding all *karma*, and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is exceedingly firm. Due to the illumination of that light of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, all worlds became the realm of universal *karma*. They merged into a single unity and entered the heart of the Buddha Vairocana, pervading the entire extent of the realm of empty space.
By virtue of the vajra-karma realm of all Tathāgatas, he became the body of Karma-Vajra and remained within the palms of the Blessed One.
At that time, from that body of Karma-Vajra, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having thus manifested, and having performed all the miraculous displays of the *karmas* of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds, because of the infinite *karmas* of all Tathāgatas and because of the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, he became the body of the Mahābodhisattva Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas. He then dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "The ritual actions (*karma*) of all Buddhas are never in vain; the Vajra of Ritual Action is able to turn [all things].
Only I, abiding here, am able to perform them extensively, accomplishing the Buddha-work through effortlessness."
At that time, the Mahābodhisattva Mahāviśvakarman descended from the heart of the Buddha and remained within the lunar disc before the Tathāgata, once again requesting instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Non-empty Vajra of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of all Tathāgatas, he turned the vast *samaya* of the infinite non-empty rituals of all *karmas*, such as offerings and so forth; for the sake of exhausting the *siddhis* of all *karmas* throughout the entire realm of sentient beings and for the enjoyment of all peace and joy; and even unto the attainment of the supreme *siddhi* of the wisdom and supernormal powers of the vajra-*karman* nature of all Tathāgatas—this Karma-Vajra became the Great Bodhisattva of Vajra-Karman for all Tathāgatas. To turn the wheel of karma for all Tathāgatas, and by means of the vajra-karma of all Tathāgatas, he conferred empowerment upon him and bestowed it into his two hands.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajraviśva and consecrated his crown with the name Vajra.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva placed that Karma-vajra upon his heart; having performed the activities of all the Tathāgatas’ karma, he proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the supreme Viśvama of all the Tathāgatas."
"I and those to whom I grant [empowerment], through the *karma* and the performer of *karma*.
This is the first wisdom regarding all the deeds performed by the Tathāgatas, belonging to the Samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Vajraviśvakarman within the Karma Family.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajra-samādhi* born of the *samaya* of the Great Bodhisattva Duryodhana-yuddha-vikrānta-vīrya; having entered it, he entered the *samaya* of the protection of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of All Tathāgatas, which issued forth from his own heart.

He then spoke these secret words: "Vajra arghaṣa. As soon as these words were spoken, from the heart of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he emerged as a firm armor, merged into a single unity, and entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Furthermore, he became a body clad in great adamantine armor and remained within the hand of the Tathāgata.
At that time, from within that body clad in adamantine armor, there emerged Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, and having performed the vast rites of protection for all Tathāgatas, their great *karmas*, and all the miraculous displays of the Tathāgatas, through the vigor of invincible combat and the extreme firmness of the Vajra-samādhi, they merged into one as a single body, the Mahābodhisattva Invincible Vigor (*Duryodhana-vīrya*).
Having attained accomplishment, he dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana and cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
"The armor formed by diligence is firm; it is more firm than other things that are firm.
Because it is firm, it is not the physical body, yet it can become the supreme vajra-body."

At that time, the Mahābodhisattva Duṣpradharṣavīrya descended from the heart of the Buddha and took his place within a moon-disc to the right of all the Tathāgatas, whereupon he again requested instruction.

At that time, the Tathāgata, having entered the samādhi of the Solid Vajra of All Tathāgatas, entered the samaya of the Vīryapāramitā of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of protecting all beings throughout the entire realm of sentient beings, for their peace, happiness, and enjoyment, and even until the attainment of the supreme siddhi-fruit of the vajra-body of all Tathāgatas, he placed that vajra armor upon the two hands of the Mahābodhisattva Durjayavīrya as described above.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the name Vajramitra and bestowed upon him the empowerment with the title "Vajra.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramitra, having donned the vajra armor for all the Tathāgatas, proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the supreme armor of compassion Of all the Tathāgatas."
"Steadfast diligence as protection is called the great kinsman.
This concludes "The Second Wisdom of the Armor of Compassionate Protection of All Tathāgatas," the Samādhi of the Great Bodhisattva Vajramitra.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra-samādhi born from the samaya of the Mahābodhisattva who Subdues All Māras; he then entered the Samaya of the Expedient Means of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of all Tathāgatas, which issued forth from his own heart.

He then uttered this secret mantra: “Vajrayakṣa. As soon as these words were spoken, [the mantra] emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Bhagavān—as a great fang-weapon, and having merged into one, it entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Having thus become a body of vajra-teeth, he remained within the palm of the Tathāgata.

At that time, from within that body of vajra-teeth, there emerged Tathāgata-bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds. Because all Tathāgatas tame the violent and wicked, because all Tathāgatas sport with miraculous transformations by utterly crushing all Māras, and because the Vajrasattva-samādhi is extremely firm, these were transformed into the bodies of Bodhisattvas who crush all Māras.
