They then dwelt within the heart of the Buddha Vairocana and uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! How marvelous!"
He said: "I am the great skillful means of all Buddhas; possessing great majestic power, I manifest in whatever form is necessary to subdue beings.
To bring about peace and benefit sentient beings, I destroy Māra and thus appear fierce and violent."
Then, that Great Bodhisattva Destroyer of Māra descended from the heart of the Buddha and, having taken his place within the lunar disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas, again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* of the Fierce Vajra of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of subduing the coarse and evil intentions of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of sentient beings, so that they might be free from fear and enjoy all peace and joy, and furthermore, to attain the supreme *siddhi*-fruit of the great skillful means, wisdom, and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas, he took that vajra-tooth weapon to destroy all Māras and bestowed it upon the Mahābodhisattva as described above with both hands.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas bestowed upon him the name Vajracaṇḍa.
Then, the Mahābodhisattva Vajracaṇḍa placed that vajra-toothed weapon into his own mouth, terrified all the Tathāgatas, and cried out these words with a loud voice:
"This is the manifestation of all Buddhas, The supreme subduer."
"The vajra-toothed weapon is established through compassionate skillful means.
This is the third [chapter], the Great Skillful Means Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, belonging to the Vajracaṇḍa Mahābodhisattva Samādhi.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the empowerment of karma born from the *samaya* of the Mahābodhisattva Fist of All Tathāgatas. He entered the *samaya* of the vajra-binding of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, which is named "The Heart of All Tathāgatas.

Having emerged from his own heart, he spoke these secret words: “Vajra-sandhi. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from those Vajradharas—he became the seal-binding (*mudrā-bandha*) of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, they merged into one and entered the heart of Vairocana Buddha.
Having been bound with the vajra-bond, they remained within the palms of the World-Honored One.
At that time, from within that Vajra-Bond body, there emerged Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, they performed all manner of miraculous transformations for the sake of the wisdom of the seals and bonds of all Tathāgatas in all worlds. Because of the firm binding by all fists and because of the extreme solidity of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single unity, becoming the body of the Mahābodhisattva Fist of All Tathāgatas.
Having been accomplished, he dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous! He said:
“I am Samaya, the one who binds the body with firmness;
though liberated, I manifest as bound so that all aspirations and requests may be accomplished.”

At that time, the body of Sarvatathāgata-muṣṭi Mahābodhisattva descended from the heart of the Buddha and dwelt within the moon-disc behind the backs of all the Tathāgatas, whereupon he again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having entered the samādhi of all Tathāgatas, bestowed the aforementioned two hands of the Vajrabandha as the Great Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi upon [the disciple]. This was for the purpose of manifesting the great supernatural power and efficacy of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of sentient beings by means of the samaya of the seals (mudrās) of all Tathāgatas; for the sake of attaining all siddhis, peace, and delightful enjoyments; and ultimately, for the sake of generating the fruit of the supreme siddhi through the seal of the omniscient wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the name Vajramuṣṭi, and further bestowed upon him the empowerment with the name Vajra.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, having bound all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-bind, proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"This is the firm vajra-bind of all the Tathāgatas."
"If one acts for the sake of all seals, because of their swift accomplishment, the samaya is extremely difficult [to master], yet karma can bring about transcendence.
This is the fourth [chapter]: "The Binding of the Body, Speech, Mind, and Wisdom of All Tathāgatas by the Great Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi Samādhi."
“Within the Karma-varga, the samādhis of the four bodhisattvas are collectively termed the ‘Karma-wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, for the sake of Vairocana Bhagavān’s entry into the wisdom-seal of all Tathāgatas, Akṣobhya Tathāgata, having entered the vajra-samādhi empowered by the vajra of the samaya of the Vajra-pāramitā, manifested from his own heart the Vajra-samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Seal of All Tathāgatas. He then spoke these secret words:”

“Sattva-vajre. As soon as these words were uttered, the vajra-light appeared from the hearts of all Tathāgatas. From the various gateways of that vajra-light—that is, from those Vajradharas—the bodies of all Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, acted as seals of omniscience; they merged into a single, unified density, pervading the entire extent of all worlds.
Having become the body of the Great Vajra, he dwelt before the World-Honored One Vairocana upon a lunar disc and proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
It is said:
"The Buddhas and the sattvas are the adamantine, which is supremely firm.
Because it is so firm, it is not a physical body, but the adamantine body."
“In the Tathāgata Family, the Vajra-pāramitā of all Tathāgatas is the foremost wisdom of the Vajra-samaya.

At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, for the sake of the World-Honored One Vairocana Tathāgata entering the Wisdom Seal of all Tathāgatas, having entered the Samādhi of the Ratna-vajra Empowerment born from the Ratna-pāramitā-samaya, immediately manifested from his heart this Body Seal of the Vajra-ratna-samaya and spoke these secret words:
‘Aro-tana-vajre. As soon as these words were spoken, jewel-like radiance emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.”

Within that Jewel Radiance—that is, that Vajradhara—one takes as many bodies of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all worlds and seals them with the wisdoms of all Tathāgatas. These merge into a single, unified density, pervading the extent of all worlds, and becoming a great Vajra-Jewel Body. Abiding within the moon disc to the right of Vairocana, he utters these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "The vajra-mudrā of all Buddhas— I am the Jewel-Vajra, the firm gateway of empowerment;
I proclaim the seal of the Tathāgata’s body."
[2] “The Second Samaya-Wisdom of the Vajra-Jewel Empowerment of All Tathāgatas within the Tathāgata Family: Jewel Pāramitā.

At that time, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to bring about the realization of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas for the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, entered the Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Samādhi born from the Dharma-Pāramitā Samaya. Immediately, he manifested from his own body this Dharma-Samaya Body-Seal and spoke these secret words:
*Dharma-vajra*. As soon as these words were uttered, lotus-light rays emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.

Within that lotus light—that is, within that Blessed One Vajradhara—he formed the wisdom-seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms of all worlds; having merged into a single, unified density, he pervaded the entire extent of all worlds.
Having become a body of vajra-lotus, he dwells within a moon disc behind the Buddha Vairocana and utters these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "All Buddhas declare me to be the Vajra of the Pure Dharma;
since my nature is pure, though I appear defiled, I am nonetheless pure."
“Thus, within the Tathāgata Family, this is the third: the Vajra-Samaya Wisdom Born from the Samaya of the Dharma-Pāramitā.

At that time, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the sake of the seal of universal gnosis (*sarvajñatā*) of the World-Honored One Vairocana and all Tathāgatas, entered the Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna-Samādhi born from the Samaya of all Pāramitās. Then, from his own heart, these seals of all Samayas emerged, and he spoke these secret words:
*Karma bhañjali*. As soon as these words were uttered, all Karma-radiance appeared from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.”
Regarding the radiance of all Tathāgatas—that is, that Blessed One Vajradhara—he [manifested] as the bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds.
Having fully aligned with the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, they again merged into a single secret union, pervading the extent of all worlds and facing the four directions.
Having become the body of the Karma-vajra, they dwelt within the moon disc to the left of the World-Honored One Vairocana, and cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: “The wisdom of all Tathāgatas, my manifold *karmas*, and the Vajra—
if these were but one— would pervade the entirety of the Buddha-worlds.”
"Able to perform the karma of activities.
"The fourth [chapter] on the wisdom of all Tathāgatas performing the Buddha-activities, the Samaya-karma-pāramitā of all Tathāgatas."
"It is named 'The Mahāpāramitā of All Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana again entered the vajra-samādhi born from the samaya of the loving worship of all Tathāgatas; then, this Mahādhīṣṭhita-devī, the retinue of all Tathāgatas, manifested from his own heart and spoke these secret words:"

"Vajra-lāsye. As soon as these words were uttered, the Vajra-mudrā emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas. At the peak of that Vajra-mudrā—namely, that Blessed One Vajradhara—having manifested as the bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all Tathāgatas, they merged into one and became the Great Vidyārājñī Vajrarati. Her entire body resembled that of a Vajrasattvī; she was adorned with exquisite colors, features, and dignified deportment, and embellished with all manner of ornaments. She is subsumed within the families of all Tathāgatas; she is the Vajrasattvī.
Once it was accomplished, he immediately took his place within a moon disc to the left of the World-Honored One Akṣobhya and cried out in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "My offering is peerless; no other is capable of it.
If one offers with love, one can perfect all offerings."
“[This is] the *Sarvatathāgata-saṃtoṣaṇa-guhyapūjā-bodhisattva-samādhi*, the foremost wisdom of the bliss and delight of all Tathāgatas.

Then, the World-Honored One again entered the *Sarvatathāgata-ratnamālā-abhiṣeka-samayodbhava-vajra-samādhi*. Thereupon, this Mahāvidyārājñī of the Sarvatathāgata family emerged from his own heart and spoke these secret words:
“Vajramale. As soon as these words were uttered, the Great Jewel Seal (*mahāratramudrā*) appeared from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

From that jewel-seal—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—having manifested as the bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, they merged into one and became the Great Goddess Vajramālā. She then took her place upon the moon-disc to the left of the Blessed One Ratnasambhava and proclaimed these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am the Treasureless One, yet I am named the Treasure of Offerings.
If one becomes the King of Supreme Truth within the triple world, one shall immediately make offerings and receive my instructions."
[This is] the second [chapter], the Jewel Garland Empowerment Offering to All Tathāgatas, concerning the Wisdom of the Factors of Enlightenment.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Vajra Samādhi born from the Song-Samaya of All Tathāgatas. From his own heart, he manifested the Mahādevī of the Family of All Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:
“Vajra-nyo-dhi. As soon as these words were uttered, the Dharma-mudrās of all Tathāgatas emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.

From that dharma-seal—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he became the bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, merging into a single unity; he then became the Mahādevī Vajragītā and, abiding within a full moon disc to the left of the Buddha Avalokiteśvararāja, uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am one who offers all these offerings as a song of praise;
though they may bring joy, they are like echoes in the void."
[This is] the third [chapter], the Samaya-Wisdom of the Gāthā-Samādhi of All Tathāgatas for the Chanting-Offering to Bodhisattvas.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called "The Birth of the Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas through the Samaya of the Dancing-Offering of All Tathāgatas," and she emerged from his own heart, immediately manifesting and speaking these secret words:
*vajra-nṛtye*. As soon as these words were uttered, she performed various vast ritual ceremonies of service as an offering to all Tathāgatas from the hearts of all Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, from that vast ritual of the dance-offering of all Tathāgatas—namely, that Blessed One Vajradhara—he manifested as Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds and dwelt within a full moon disc to the left of the Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata, proclaiming these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: “The vast and great single offering is the offering to all; it can bring benefit throughout the entire world.
If one employs the ritual of the vajra dance, one will be able to accomplish the worship of the Buddha.”
"Thus concludes the fourth [section]: the Wisdom of the Ritual Action (*karmajñāna*) for the Dance Offering to All Tathāgatas, which is the unsurpassed offering to all Tathāgatas.
The above four sections constitute the secret dharma offerings of all the Tathāgatas."

At that time, the Bhagavān Akṣobhya, in order to further honor Vairocana Tathāgata through external offerings, entered the samādhi called "The Adamantine Birth of the Samaya that Causes All Tathāgatas to Flourish. From his own heart, he brought forth the Mistress of Incense of All Tathāgatas, named Sarvatathāgatādhipativajrā, and spoke these secret words:

*Vajra-dūpi*. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas—that is, from that very Bhagavān Vajradhara—there arose an immeasurable, manifold cloud of various ornaments and offerings that gathered together.

When these immeasurable clouds of incense, vapors, and arrays of clouds had completely filled the entire Vajradhātu, further, from that ocean of clouds of incense offerings and arrays, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerged. These merged into a single, dense unity to form the body of the Vajra Incense Goddess (*Vajragandhadevī*). She dwelt within a moon disc at the left corner of the Lord Akṣobhya’s Vajramaṇi-peak pavilion and uttered these words in a loud voice:
“How marvelous!”
He said: "I am the offering for the devas, able to cause all that is good to flourish;
if I enter into all sentient beings, they shall swiftly realize Bodhi."
“‘The first is the Vajra-Gathering Wisdom born from the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s Incense Offering that Causes All Tathāgatas to Flourish.

At that time, the World-Honored One Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to further honor the World-Honored One Vairocana through external offerings, entered the Vajra-Samādhi born from the Samaya of the Jewel-Adornment Offering. From his own heart, he manifested the Goddess who Carries the Commands of All Tathāgatas and spoke this secret mantra:
‘Vajra Puṣpe. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there arose the adornment of all flower offerings.”

Having appeared and pervaded the entirety of space, there further emerged from the midst of all the floral offerings and adornments bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds. These merged into a single, dense unity to form the body of the Vajra-Command-Receiving Goddess (Vajrājñākarī), who dwelt within a moon disc at the left corner of the Vairocana World-Honored One’s Vajra-Maṇi-Peak Pavilion, and proclaimed these words with a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am this flower offering, capable of serving as all manner of ornaments;
having made this offering to the Jewel-Nature, may I swiftly attain Bodhi."
"The second Samaya-jñāna: the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Vajrapuṣpa-pūjā of All Tathāgatas, and the Samādhi of the Jewel Ornament Pūjā of All Tathāgatas."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to make offerings to the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the vajra-samādhi born from the samaya of the light-offering of all Tathāgatas, following external modes of worship. Then, this female messenger of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart and uttered this secret mantra:
“Vajraloke. As soon as these words were spoken, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there arose the adornment of the light-offering for all worlds.

Having manifested pervading the entire *dharmadhātu*, from within all those light-offering adornments, there further appeared Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds. These merged into one, forming the body of the Vajra-light Radiant Tathāgata. He then dwelt within a moon disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajra-maṇi-peak Pavilion and uttered these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said:
"I am the Great Offering; as a lamp of purity, if one possesses the light of the Dharma, one will swiftly attain the eye of all Buddhas."
"The Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Adornment of Offerings with the Lamp-Light of All Tathāgatas," also known as "The Third: The Wisdom of the Tathāgata’s Light Pervading the Dharma Realm."

"At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, in order to make offerings to the World-Honored One Vairocana by means of external offerings, entered the vajra-samādhi born from the samaya of the offering of ointment of all Tathāgatas. Having done so, he brought forth from his own heart the female servants of all Tathāgatas and spoke these secret words:"

"Vajra-gandhe. As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there appeared the adornment of the incense offering of all Tathāgatas. From within those adornments of the incense offerings of all [Tathāgatas], there further appeared bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, which merged into one to become the body of the deity Vajragandhā. She dwelt within the moon disc at the left corner of the Lord’s Vajramaṇi-śikhara Pavilion and cried out in a loud voice:
"How wonderful! (Aho!)"
He said: "I offer this unguent, which is exquisite and pleasing;
if one were to apply the fragrance of the Tathāgata universally to all bodies."

"This is the fourth [wisdom], the samādhi of the Bodhisattva Samaya of the Incense Offering of All Tathāgatas, which is the wisdom of the incense of the precepts, samādhi, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas."
“The goddess named Sarvatathāgataśāsana-sampratīcchikā.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata, again entered the *samādhi* of the Sattvavajra born from the *samaya-hook* (*samayāṅkuśa*) of all Tathāgatas. From his own heart, he manifested this Lord of Seals (*mudrādhipati*) of the entire assembly of all Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:

‘Vajra-kusaja’ (with a short vowel). As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there appeared the entire assembly of seals of all Tathāgatas. From those [seals], Tathāgata bodies emerged, equal in number to the atoms of all worlds of all Tathāgatas, and they merged into one.”

Having further manifested as the body of the Vajrāṅkuśa Mahābodhisattva, he dwelt within the moon disc at the center of the Vajra in the Seṇḍaka Pavilion of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiśikhara, and having bound all Tathāgatas to their samaya, he cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: “I am the Tathāgatas, the firm samaya;
once I have summoned you, you shall reverently serve all maṇḍalas.”
“[This is] the first wisdom of the hook-summoning of all Tathāgatas through the *Sarvatathāgatāṅkuśa-bodhisattva-samādhi*.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *Sarvatathāgata-samayapraveśa-mahābodhisattva-samayasambhava-samādhi*. From his own heart, he manifested the messenger who leads all Tathāgatas into the seal (*mudrā*), and then spoke these secret words:”

"Vajra-paśya! (pronounced with a short vowel). As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—having caused the multitudes of seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas to enter, there appeared from those multitudes of seals of all Tathāgatas bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, which then merged into one.

Furthermore, he manifested as the body of the Vajrapāśa Mahābodhisattva and dwelt within a moon disc at the jeweled gate of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiśikhara Pavilion; having summoned all the Tathāgatas, he cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am all the Tathāgatas, the adamantine and firm noose;
even if one enters into all atoms, I shall cause them to be drawn back in."
"Chapter Two: Entering the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas’ Vajrapāśa Mahābodhisattva and the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the Samādhi of the Sattvavajra Born from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva of All Tathāgatas’ Samayāṅkuśa; immediately, from his own heart, he manifested the Messenger who binds the hearts of all Tathāgatas, and spoke these secret words:"

“Vajra-sphoṭa! As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—he emerged as the multitude of seals of the samaya-bonds of all Tathāgatas. Furthermore, from within those multitudes of seals of the samaya-bonds of all Tathāgatas, there appeared bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, which merged into a single, unified whole.

Having become the body of the Mahābodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa-lakṣa, he dwelt within a moon disc amidst the gateway of the Tathāgata’s Vajramaṇiratna-śikhara-kūṭāgāra dharma-door, and cried out these words in a loud voice:
"How marvelous!"
He said: "I am all the Tathāgatas, the adamantine, firm hook and chain;
though all bonds are liberated, I undergo bondage for the sake of sentient beings."
"The third [chapter] on the Wisdom of the Binding Samaya of All Tathāgatas: the Samādhi of the Mahābodhisattva Samaya-Chain of All Tathāgatas."

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Sattvavajra Born from the Mahābodhisattva-Samaya of the Incorporation of All Tathāgatas; immediately, from his own heart, he manifested these servants of the seals (mudrā) of all Tathāgatas and spoke these secret words:

“Vajraveśa” (pronounced with a short vowel). As soon as these words were uttered, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas—that is, from that Blessed One Vajradhara—there emerged a multitude of mantras belonging to all the Tathāgatas. From within that multitude of mantras of all the Tathāgatas, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds appeared; they merged into one and became the body of the Vajra-Entrance. Abiding within the moon disc at the gateway of the karma-section of the Blessed One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, he cried out in a loud voice: “How marvelous!”
He said:
"I am all the Tathāgatas; firmly grasped by the vajra, I can act as the lord of all, and yet also serve as their servant."

"Thus ends the fourth [chapter], the Wisdom of the Vajra-Inclusion of All Tathāgatas, titled 'The Vajra-Samādhi Arising from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva, into which all Tathāgatas are Included.'"
"All those mentioned above are called the recipients of the teachings of all Tathāgatas.

Following the sequence as previously described, one should contemplate the original samādhi, personal form, attire, and the symbolic seals (mudrās) held by each of the entire assembly of retinues, the masters of the maṇḍala, and all the bodhisattvas headed by Vajrasattva; thereafter, one should contemplate the physical characteristics of the Lord Bodhisattva of the Mantra whom one personally upholds."
Furthermore, one should visualize all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, filling the realm of empty space, as numerous as sesame seeds.

If one sits with legs crossed, placing the right hand upon the left, and presses the tongue against the upper palate, one should fix the mind upon the tip of the nose at the subtle vajra-pillar. Binding the mind with the rope of mindfulness, one makes it pliant and serviceable; like refined and purified wax, the mind becomes compliant and fit for various applications.
Furthermore, just as rock crystal, mica, and the like are by nature transparent and clear, manifesting transformations according to the colors and shadows cast upon them;

so too is this mind. Its intrinsic nature is pure, yet through deluded karma and attachment to worldly arts and crafts, it undergoes transformation according to those influences, becoming adorned with all manner of false conceptualizations.

"It would be better to turn from delusion toward the true, cultivating the reality-mark (*dharmatā*), the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), supreme merit, and the analytical application of the path.

Thus, with the flavor of decisive wisdom, skillful intention, and courageous majesty, one observes the distractions of one's own mind—the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements permeated by afflictions, along with their grasped objects and grasping subjects—which arise in association with the selflessness of phenomena (*dharmanairātmya*). These are like a mirage, a magical illusion, a city of the *gandharvas*, an echo in the sky, a whirling firebrand, or a false dream; they are far removed from more than one hundred and sixty worldly states of mind."

Having reflected thus, one gains self-evident knowledge within one's own body and mind: "That which has been truly spoken by those who know the Way and see the Way is not understood by foolish people who are bound and attached to signs."

"Next, one must enter into contemplation and cease the inhalation and exhalation of the breath. Initially, one relies on the yoga of *ānāpāna* (mindfulness of breathing) to practice the fixing of mindfulness; without moving the body nor moving the limbs, this is called the *aśvāsapraśvāsaka* method."

When one who has long practiced meditation reflects in this way, they enter a state of perception wherein they see themselves dwelling in space, while all Buddhas pervade the entire Dharma-realm; then, by means of the finger-snap mudrā, [the Buddhas] cause them to rise from their seat.
“The reciter should contemplate and listen attentively as all the Buddhas declare:
‘O son of noble family!
You should quickly realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.’”
"If you have not yet fully understood the reality of all Tathāgatas, how can you endure and practice all these ascetic hardships?
At that time, having heard the words of all the Buddhas, he immediately emerged from meditative absorption according to the prescribed ritual and performed the mudrā for rising from one's seat.

As for the method of this mudrā: having formed the double vajra-fists, hook the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *sūcī* (middle finger) fingers together, and let the *madhyamā* (index finger) and *anāmikā* (ring finger) fingers rest facing upward against one another.

Then, recite the secret mantra: "Oṃ vajra tiṣṭha. Having arisen with this mudrā, one should visualize the ocean of Buddhas of the ten directions, and before each Buddha, imagine oneself standing at their feet, prostrating to all the Tathāgatas.
When the ritual is completed, one should recite this secret mantra as follows:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittapraṇāma vajrapāṇi hūṃ karomi. [The Sanskrit preserves the initial syllable.]
The treatise says:
"With the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, I, this Vajra, pay homage.
Having paid homage to all Tathāgatas in succession, he spoke these words:
"I pray that the World-Honored One will instruct me:
what is the true Dharma?
How should one dwell in it and practice it?"
Furthermore, one should reflect that all Tathāgatas address one from each direction, saying these words:
"O son of noble family!
You should achieve the intrinsic nature of samādhi and perform the recitation according to your intention; you must observe your own mind."
He then spoke the secret mantra:
“Oṃ citta-prativedhaṃ kuru. While reciting this secret mantra, having visualized one’s own mind as being like a lunar disc, he further addressed all the Tathāgatas:
“World-Honored Ones!...”
"I pray that you will instruct me, for I wish to see the form of the lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas replied once more:
"O son of noble family!
This mind is pure by nature; it adapts to whatever it is employed for and is capable of fulfilling any purpose at will, just as a plain garment easily takes on dye.
Because the mind increases wisdom through its naturally pure nature, one should generate the bodhicitta by means of the mantras accomplished through that very nature.
He then spoke these secret words:
“Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. While reciting these words, one should perform the vajra-bond mudrā.

By means of this secret mantra, one should immediately visualize that lunar disc as being extremely pure and firm, produced by great merit, arising from the Buddha-nature and Bodhi; its shape is like a lunar disc, tranquil, pure, and free from all defilements.
“The Buddhas and the sons of the Buddha proclaim the name of the bodhicitta; having beheld the moon formed by wisdom, they then address and reveal it to all the Tathāgatas:
‘World-Honored One!...’”
"I see that moon-disc as utterly pure.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas said to him:
"You should draw near to the Samantabhadra-mind of all the Tathāgatas; you should skillfully cultivate this Samantabhadra-mind of all the Tathāgatas, because it is firm and stable."
Within the moon disc of one’s own mind, visualize the form of a vajra, dull-golden in color and emitting blazing rays of light; this is the stainless, pure wisdom of the Buddha.

"Furthermore, one should visualize that the mallet possesses five-pronged tongs. The master who recites the mantra, following the instructions of all Buddhas, should visualize the seal of the five-pronged tongs placed within the mallet and recite the secret mantra: *Tiṣṭha vajra*.

Next, the method for binding the seal is explained: having first performed the *vajrabandha*, one extends the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (little finger) fingers so they touch, and raises the *vīrya* (middle) fingers beside the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers like curved tongs, with a distance between them equal to two barley grains."
Furthermore, by joining the *samādhi-pāramitā* and the *dāna-prajñā-pāramitā* two by two, held upright like the prongs of a fork, these are called the five Vajra-mudrās.

Next, the practitioner of yoga again employs the Vajra-karma-mudrā; visualizing this Vajra-seal as being extensively expanded, he utters the secret mantra: *Sapara vajra*. Regarding the method for binding the Karma-mudrā:

with the *samādhi-pāramitā* and *prajñā-pāramitā*, one pinches the tips of the *dāna-pāramitā* and *upāya-pāramitā* respectively, extending the remaining three fingers like a three-pronged *vajra*. With the left hand facing upward and the right hand facing downward, placing the right over the left at the level of the heart, one rubs and rotates them like a wheel.

"Next, one should visualize one's own mind as the bodhicitta and one's body as being composed of vajra. Reciting the aforementioned secret mantra with mental concentration, one should then, according to one's own will, fully extend the vajra-body until it fills all worlds throughout the entirety of space."
"Next, one should bind that vajra with this mantra;
thus, the mantra is spoken: OṂ SAṄKHARA VAJRA. Next, that vajra is made firm by this mantra; furthermore, the mantra is spoken:
OṂ NIRĪTA TIṢṬHA VAJRA. Having made it firm with this spell, the body is maintained as before."

"Next, one should contemplate that within the entire realm of space, all the vajra realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas are empowered by the spiritual power of the Buddhas and enter into the vajra of one's own body."
While forming this thought, recite the secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajratāma-ju-haṃ samayahaṃ mahāsamayahaṃ sarvatathāgata-abhisambodhi-vajra-tāma-ju-haṃ. [The Sanskrit preserves the initial syllable.]
The treatise states:
"I am the vajra-body, the samaya-body, and the mahāsamaya-body; all Tathāgatas, having manifested and realized awakening, constitute the vajra-body."

"Next, with a mind of single-minded concentration, one should visualize one's own body as being adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence (lakṣaṇa-vyañjana), draped in interwoven silken garments, receiving empowerment with the crowns of all Buddhas, and visualizing oneself as the body of a Mahābodhisattva."

"Next, because one desires to transcend the firm physical forms of the various devas, one should properly contemplate this ritual: the empowerment and consecration through the samādhi of the deity recited by oneself."
Next is the method for forming the mudrā: having firmly bound the *vajrabandha*, extend straight out the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers.

For the sake of yogic empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), one should place this seal upon the heart; then, [place them] successively on the forehead, the throat, and the crown of the head, while reciting the secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasattva adhiṣṭhasva sarvamāṃ. By means of this yoga, empower oneself as a *vajra*; for all empowerment seals, follow the respective *kula*.
Having placed it in its position, one unties it at the crown of the head and recites the mantra one has been chanting.
Regarding the "divine consecration" (*devābhiṣeka*): it refers to placing the Vajraratnamudrā, which arises from the heart, upon the forehead as a consecration.

Regarding the method for binding the empowerment mudrā: having bound the vajra-bond, extend the wisdom and concentration fingers; bring the tips of the forefinger and middle finger together; and bend their middle joints so that they resemble the shape of a maṇi jewel. This is called the empowerment-bestowing mudrā.
Then he spoke these secret words:
“Oṃ vajra-aratnābhiṣekamahe. Next, one should contemplate the deity of the mantra one is reciting as entering into one’s own body, and recite these four syllables of the secret words:
“Hūṃ raṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Through the empowerment of this yoga, all mantras and mudrās will swiftly attain accomplishment.

Next, regarding what the Bodhisattva Vajradhara taught: having separated the mudrās of consecration, each retains its original force; one performs three circumambulations with the hands joined at the forehead using the *jinru* (victory) gesture, according to the method for binding a garland;
the same is done behind the crown of the head.
Having completed the binding, one should sequentially loosen and untie it from the two sides of the crown, proceeding down to the abdomen via the *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers.
Recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-aratnamale abhiṣiñca sarvamunirāja-nirdeśa-hilokamalakapavana vaṃ. The remaining empowerment mudrās are to be loosened using this same method.
Next, bind the Vajrabandha-applause mudrā to cause joy, and then recite the secret mantra:
“Oṃ vajra doḥhiḥ. By means of this verbal method, release the bound seal and cause [the deity] to attain joy; one shall then become the vajra-nature, or Vajrasattva.

"This yoga method is for the sixteen Mahāsattvas, as well as Maitreya and others who have attained mastery in the various ten stages (*daśabhūmi*). Those great Bodhisattvas are each empowered and consecrated by their respective *samaya-mudrā* and other samādhis; one should contemplate and practice the sequence according to the aforementioned method."

"If one further recites the mantras of the Tathāgata family, or recites those of the Cakravartin, one should perform empowerment and consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna-abhiṣeka*) according to the methods explained below.
Regarding the empowerment through the yoga of all families: having formed the *sattvavajra-mudrā*, one places it upon the heart according to the method for binding the seal."
Having formed the vajra-bond, one extends the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers upright like needles.
Then, recite the mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasattva ātiṣṭha svāhā hūṃ. This is called the *mudrā* for the empowerment of the Vajra Family.
"Furthermore, if one belongs to the Ratna Family, one should bind the Vajra-Ratna Mudrā.
Regarding the method for binding this mudrā: having first formed the Vajra-bandha, one should pinch the surfaces of the thumbs (jñāna-samādhi fingers) together, slightly bending them;
then, with the middle fingers (kṣānti-praṇidhāna fingers), one pinches the surfaces together, curving them downward like a jewel."
Placing it upon the forehead, one recites the secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-aratna-adhiṣṭhā-svāhaṃ-tara. This is called the mudrā of the empowerment of the Vajra-Jewel of the Jewel Family.
"Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.

As for the method of binding this mudrā: having formed the Vajra-bond, extend the *kṣemavīrya* (ring) fingers slightly curved so that they touch one another like lotus petals. Place it beneath the nape of the neck and empower it.
Then recite the mantra: 'Oṃ vajrapadmādhiṣṭhāpaya mama hṛdaye. This is called the empowerment-phrase-seal (*adhiṣṭhāna-vāk-mudrā*) of the Lotus Family."
"Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Karma-kula.

As for the method of binding this mudrā: form the Vajra-bandha, bend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhāna* (little finger) fingers into the palms, and extend the *tarjanī* (forefinger), *madhyamā* (middle finger), *jñāna* (third finger), and *samādhi* (pinky) fingers upright like needles.
Place it upon the crown of the head and perform the empowerment, reciting the secret mantra: 'Oṃ vajrakarmādhiṣṭhānasamayam aḥ. This is called the empowerment-mantra and mudrā of the Karma-kula."
"Furthermore, the sequential initiation rites for all the families are explained.
For the Vajra Family: having performed the vajrasattva-bond as described above, place it before the crown of the head to perform self-initiation, and recite this mantra:
*Oṃ vajrābhiṣiñca māṃ hūṃ*. For the Ratna Family: form the ratnasamaya-mudrā as described above, place it on the right side of the crown to perform self-initiation, and recite this mantra:"
"Oṃ vajra-aratna-abhiṣiñca māṃ tra. For the Lotus Family, form the Lotus Samaya-mudrā as described above; place it behind the crown of the head to perform self-consecration, and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-padma-abhiṣiñca māṃ hre. For the Karma Family, form the Karma Samaya-seal as described above; place it on the right side of the crown to perform self-consecration, and recite this mantra:

"Oṃ vajra-karma-abhiṣiñca māṃ na. Having thus performed the consecration as described above, recite the aforementioned four-syllable mantra according to the previous method to cause it to enter one's own body.

"Furthermore, as previously described, one should bind the initiation garland upon one's own head and abide sequentially in yoga. Each person, according to the mudrā of their respective family, should arrange the wings of śamatha and vipaśyanā as described above; maintaining the force of the fundamental mudrā, they should bind the initiation garland upon their crown, circling it three times around the forehead and the back of the head as before. Others should all follow this example."
"Having formed the *sattvavajra* mudrā of the Vajra Family, one should divide it into two and bind a garland made of pure vajras upon one's own head, reciting this mantra:

*Oṃ vajramālā abhiṣiñca māṃ haṃ vaṃ*. Having formed the *ratnavajra* mudrā of the Ratna Family, one should divide it into two and bind a garland made of various jewels upon one's own head, reciting this mantra: *Oṃ vajraratna*."

*Mali abhiṣiñca māṃ vaṃ.* [The Lotus Family: Having formed the Vajra Mudrā of the Binding Law, divide it into two; one should fasten a garland produced from all dharmas upon one’s own head and recite this secret mantra:

*Oṃ vajradharma mali abhiṣiñca māṃ vaṃ.* [The Karma Family: Having formed the Karma Vajra Mudrā, divide it into two; one should fasten a garland produced from all karma upon one’s own head and recite this secret mantra:
*Oṃ vajrakarma mali abhiṣiñca māṃ vaṃ.* Next, as previously described for the consecration garland, one should place the Vajradhātviśvarī Mudrā of all Tathāgatas at the crown of the head.

Regarding the method for this mudrā: having formed the vajra-bind mudrā, extend the two *kṣānti* (patience) fingers so that their tips slightly touch, and place the two *vīrya* (effort) fingers outside the initial joint of the *kṣānti* fingers.

Then, recite this secret mantra: “Oṃ sarvatathāgata-abhisambodhi-vajrābhiṣeka-maṃ haṃ vaṃ. Next, visualize yourself adorned with the jeweled crowns of all the Tathāgatas, and as before, recite the four-syllable secret mantra:
“Rāṃ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. By reciting these words, cause all the Tathāgatas to enter your own body.
Next, bind the Vajrabandha mudrā as before, clapping the hands together to cause joy, and recite this secret mantra:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhisambodhivajrasvabhāvātmako ’ham. Having thus adorned oneself with the various mudrās of the body, speech, and mind-vajra of all Tathāgatas, one should again visualize and contemplate that one’s own form is likewise adorned. Then, to make it firm, recite the hundred-syllable secret mantra of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of all Tathāgatas. It is as follows: “Oṃ... [The hundred syllables follow].

Vajrasattva-samaya-mānu-pālaya | Vajrasattva-samaya māṃ rakṣa | Vajrasattva-tvena upatiṣṭha | Vajrasattva-nirdeśena māṃ bhava | Dr̥ḍho me bhava | Sutoshyo me bhava | Anurakto me bhava | Supoṣyo me bhava | Anurakto me bhava.

*Sarvasiddhi-han-maṃ para-ya-ccho dadāhi me sarva-siddhiṃ sarva-karma-su-ca-maṃ ca sarva-karmāṇi ca | Citta-śrīye māṃ rakṣa kuru hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ bhagavan bhagavat sarva-tathāgata-vajra-mayi mañca mā vajra muñca māṃ vajri bhava | Māṃ kuru vajra-samaya-sattva mahā-samaya-sattva āḥ.* Having thus made [the commitment] firm, one is empowered by the body, speech, and mind-vajras of all the Tathāgatas, and visualizes oneself as having attained perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*).
Next, one should offer oneself before all the Tathāgatas and recite this secret mantra:

"Oṃ yathā sarvatathāgata-tathatvam, tathāham. Furthermore, with a mind of right concentration, one should observe from above the self's body and mind, and the entire true *mahābodhicitta*, which is produced by various merits adorned with the categories of form, established through skillful means, and embellished by the intention to rescue and deliver the entirety of the world, forever remaining far removed from all conceptual discrimination.
Having visualized as above, one should then recite this secret mantra:

“Oṃ tathāgata-hṛdaya-m-aham-asmi tathāgata. Furthermore, I have now entered the stage of the conduct of Samantabhadra Mahābodhisattva; I have realized non-abiding nirvāṇa and accomplished the marvelous, such that my own supreme realization cannot be fully described.
"I now pay homage to all Tathāgatas and address them, saying: 'Bhagavān!
May you empower me to realize manifest complete enlightenment; may you make it firm.'"
Having made this supplication, one should visualize all the Tathāgatas entering into the *sattvavajra* within one’s own heart and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhisambodhiniṣṭhādhṛtisaṃbhava-vajra tiṣṭha. [From] the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-saṃkṣipta-paṭala-nāma-vidhi*, Scroll Two. [End of] Scroll Two.
[From] the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-saṃkṣipta-paṭala-nāma-vidhi*, Scroll Two. [End of] Scroll Two.
Furthermore, one should reflect in this way: [Translated by Vajrabodhi, Tripitaka Master of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty] "Furthermore, one should reflect in this way:"

"Not long after I attained perfect enlightenment, I was consecrated by the Samantabhadra-mind of all Tathāgatas and the great maṇi-jewel born of the space of all Tathāgatas. I obtained the dharma-wisdom-pāramitā of Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas; and through the non-empty and unobstructed nature of the Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas, the goals sought as the basis for my teachings were all fully accomplished and perfected."

I should now wander throughout the entire realm of phenomena, pervading all worlds within the ocean of clouds that fills the entirety of space. For the sake of realizing the equal-nature wisdom and all spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas, and for the sake of all sentient beings in every established location within each world, I should generate the great bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, accomplish the state of Samantabhadra, perform various services to the families of all Tathāgatas, and proceed to the site of the Great Bodhi-maṇḍala.

One should manifest the subduing of all māra armies and realize the *mahābodhi* of the wisdom of equality of all Tathāgatas; one should turn the wheel of Dharma, subdue all non-Buddhists, and even provide universal protection and refuge for all sentient beings; one should bestow upon them various forms of peace and joy, and accomplish the supreme *siddhi* of the *sarvajñajñāna* and the supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas; furthermore, by means of various analogies for all sentient beings, one should manifest as a youth playing in the royal palace, escaping the city to renounce the world, appearing to practice austerities, and having non-Buddhists come to my presence.
"Furthermore, one should reflect:

'The miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas shall again be manifested; yet I have not yet attained complete freedom from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*). Therefore, I must resolutely employ the power born of the samādhis of all Tathāgatas—which can manifest all that is pure and all worldly conceptual proliferation—for the sake of purifying all worlds.'"

One should observe all the maṇḍalas to be constructed within the maṇḍala of the Tathāgata family by means of this method; therein, one should sit according to the ritual rules and practice the empowerment of oneself, thereby forming the seal of the Mahābodhisattva—the so-called seal of Vajrasattva.

"Having been empowered by this seal-dharma (*mudrā-vidhi*), one should arise; forming a vajra-fist with the left hand, one visualizes the right hand as a vajra, assumes a majestic and fierce appearance, and while observing all directions universally, one should press down upon it while reciting 'I am Vajrasattva'."

Regarding the place where the altar is constructed—whether it be a separate purified chamber or an existing purified chamber—the methods for selecting the site and so forth do not differ from those explained in the Susiddhi [Tantra]. Furthermore, the application of cow dung (*gomaya*) for purifying the ground should be performed according to the usual procedure.

"Next, having twisted together the various strands of rope until they are firm and perfectly arranged, and having measured them according to the length of an elbow, the wise one should, according to his strength, use the rope to mark out the mandala."

The altar is square in shape with four gates adorned with the four auspicious symbols. It is provided with four boundary lines of cord, and silk fabrics, banners, and canopies are suspended to adorn its various corners. The gateways are divided by projecting arches, and the outer altar ground is marked out with alternating patterns of vajra-jewels.
"If one acts as a sovereign king of Jambudvīpa or as a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin), the maṇḍala should be drawn with a circumference exceeding one yojana;
for a master of great majesty and virtue, it may be gradually reduced in size, even down to a measurement of four cubits."
When a wise person observes that a candidate is fit for conversion, they may establish a maṇḍala according to their own judgment without fault.

Desiring to benefit those who should be converted, Vajrasattva established the maṇḍalas known as the Vajradhātu and others; as described in the sūtras, these may even be set within the palm of one's hand.
One may perform all those maṇḍalas at will and they will bring benefit; how much more so on the ground?

Regarding the method for a four-cubit maṇḍala: the eaves on each of the four sides shall be twelve finger-widths wide. Within it, one should spread colored powders and paint the Bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa, such as Maitreya, Ajita, and others, as well as the gatekeepers and the attendants, with a width of ten and a half fingers, or one barleycorn plus a half.
The measurement of those gates should take one-ninth of four cubits; the entrance to the gate is slightly wider.
If the master who draws the maṇḍala follows this method in drawing it, he will cause all the mahāsattvas to be filled with joy.

"Outside the door, one must measure according to the width of the doorway; taking half of that measurement as the base, one should add a further length equal to it. Each of these should be bent across horizontally, measured evenly as above, and each marked with vertical lines. Looking from both sides, the horizontal lines form the junction."
Take one-third of one side of its outer perimeter and circle it from the heart to form a wheel.
Again, take one-third of its middle portion and circle it upward from the heart to form a wheel.

"In the center of that maṇḍala is the gate-tower wheel; eight lines are drawn horizontally and vertically below it. Visualize *vajras* like pillars of a palace to form eight columns, adorning the great circular wheel; these are also *vajra* images made in five colors, numbering either one hundred and eight or thirty-seven, with their sharp points joined together, extending from the entrance gate to the northeast corner where the auspicious gate-pillars are erected."

"Having thus drawn the outer maṇḍala according to this method, the wise one enters its central palace, which resembles a moon disc, and arranges the lines of the vajra-path. Adorned with eight pillars erected upon vajra-columns, one should place an image of the Buddha within each of the five moon discs at the center of the inner maṇḍala. Furthermore, one should sequentially paint the four supreme Samaya-deities on the four sides of the Buddha and at the center of each of the various maṇḍalas."

Furthermore, one should split [the space] with the vajra-force and enter the four mandalas. Regarding the "vajra-force": it consists of mentally lifting up that which has been drawn and the vajra-line. Whether entering or exiting, the person drawing the mandala must not step over the path of the vajra-line; they should lift it by reciting the mantra and pass beneath it, thereby not violating the samaya.
Then he spoke this secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajrāvega kara hūṃ. "The four Buddhas, beginning with Akṣobhya, should all be arranged [therein]."

First, from the vajra direction, one draws the mandala of Akṣobhya, complete with the four supreme Samaya deities such as Vajradhara. One should visualize the Buddhas of the four directions facing toward the seat of Vairocana. First, draw Vajradhara in front of Akṣobhya; next, to the right; then to the left; and finally behind.
The other families follow this same procedure.

"Next, one arrives at the Ratna-direction Ratnasaṃbhava maṇḍala, with Pūrṇavajragarbha and others; next, the Padma-direction Amitābha maṇḍala, with Viśuddhavajranetra and others; and the Karma-direction Amoghasiddhi maṇḍala, with Vajraviśva and others."
Within the Vaṃbu [Maṇḍala], place the four Pāramitās according to their respective original directions.
Within the wheel, place the four inner offerings in the four corners, beginning from the direction of Agni and proceeding clockwise until reaching the direction of Īśāna.
Within the lines at the four corners of the outer mandala, place the outer offerings; the ritual procedure is the same as before.

Furthermore, outside the four corners, draw half-vajras, and between the four gates, paint the four gatekeepers who gather [beings]. Within the center of the outer mandala, one should place Mahāsattva, complete with all marks, who is capable of providing all benefits.
The Vajrācārya, who fully understands the ritual procedures, should paint the heads of the deities with an undistracted mind.

If one lacks the capacity to paint them, one may instead paint the respective mudrās of each family using various pigments; these should all be placed upon the heads of the deities who possess supreme merit. Using powdered precious gems as pigment—or various *dhātu* powders such as vermilion, malachite, and azurite—or else finely ground rice flour dyed in the five exquisite colors, one should first apply the colors starting from the interior: first white, then red, then yellow and green; these shall all be within the inner court.
“The outer enclosure is made black; within each of the five colors, one should visualize the addition of a syllable:

in the white color, visualize the syllable VAṂ; in the red color, visualize placing the syllable YAM; in the yellow color, visualize the syllable ĀLAṂ; in the green color, visualize the syllable LAṂ; and in the black color, visualize the syllable HAṂ.”

"Once these five syllables have been placed within each of the colors, one should contemplate therein the five kinds of Tathāgata wisdom—namely, the wisdom of the nature of the *dharmadhātu*. With a mind of great compassion, for the sake of causing all those in the world who are submerged in the mud of afflictions and addicted to the pleasures of the five desires to turn back from them, one should practice yoga-contemplation, thinking:
'I shall establish [beings] in the five kinds of Tathāgata wisdom.'"
"Having bound this seal, touch each of the five colors with it. As for the method of binding it:
extend the two forefingers of two vajra-fists so that they face upward and are pressed against each other like needles."
Then he spoke this secret mantra:

"Oṃ vajracittasamaya. While reciting this secret mantra, one should gaze at it with clear eyes; if one wishes for its color to appear blazing and radiant, one should empower it with a sincere vow, saying:

"These sentient beings are deeply attached to colors. Furthermore, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the Buddhas follow their attachments and desires through the power of truthful speech, so that these colors and other qualities all blaze forth with radiance."
"This method of binding the maṇḍala should be performed using colored powder; this is the most excellent. If one desires it to be long-lasting and stable, it may also be executed by painting.
Next, the method for drawing the mudrās is explained:
within the *vaṃ*-wheel maṇḍala, draw a lotus pedestal, upon which place a stūpa; this is called the Vajradhātu-īśvara-mudrā."

On the lotus seat within the maṇḍala of the eastern direction of Śakra, one should draw a horizontal vajra, with a vertical vajra atop the horizontal one; this is called the Vajra Heart Seal (Vajrahṛdayamudrā).
On the flower seat within the maṇḍala of the southern direction of Yama, one places a precious jewel; this is called the Self-Body Empowerment Seal (Svadeha-abhiṣekamudrā).
Within the maṇḍala of the northern direction of the Nāgas, one draws a horizontal vajra with a lotus flower drawn above it; this is the Dharma Weapon Seal (Dharmapratīhāramudrā).
On the flower seat of the Yakṣa Square Wheel Maṇḍala, one should draw the form of the Karma-vajra in the shape of a cross, with all its edges sharp as blades; this is called the Seal of All Vajras.
All seals (mudrā) that are painted must possess a halo and be placed upon a lotus.
Furthermore, in the primary position of the Vajra Family, paint the seal of Vajrasattva: draw two vajras standing side by side, with their upper and lower prongs mutually interlaced.
Next, draw two *vajras* shaped like arrows.
Next, draw one labeled "Excellent" (*sādhu*), forming a fist as if snapping the fingers.
Next, draw a jewel within the palm, complete with radiant flames.
Next, draw the Vajra-Sun Disc mudrā, with radiant flames as described above.
Next, draw a jeweled banner (*ratnadhvaja*), upon which flames are depicted.
Next, draw two crossed vajras (*viśvavajra*) horizontally, and in their center, draw an image with bared teeth.
Next, draw a vajra with lotuses at its waist and vajra-swords and -daggers, complete with blazing light.
Next, draw the spokes of a vajra-wheel, and then draw its tongue, endowed with brilliant radiance.
Next, draw Karma-vajra, with heads and faces on all sides; draw a horizontal vajra, upon which is a half-vajra.
Next, the image of the armor, with the form of a half-gada at the collar and sleeves;
next, draw a horizontal gada, above which are two fangs.
Next, draw a horizontal vajra with two vajra-fists above it.

Next, draw the seal of the sign of accomplishment for Sattvavajra and the others; one should draw Vajrarati and so forth, and furthermore, outside of that, draw their respective seals according to the ritual procedure.
Furthermore, between the gates, one should draw the seals (mudrās) of the gatekeepers; as with the previously described seal-images, each shall have a lotus flower below and a blaze of light above.
"Next, draw the self-seals (*svamudrā*) of Maitreya and the others; all those who are to be drawn may be depicted according to one's preference.
Furthermore, visualize a thousand bodhisattvas in each of the various directions, all fully adorned, and establish them by means of their respective verbal seals (*vāṅmudrā*)."

"Then, standing before the entrance of the maṇḍala and having carefully observed it all around, one should apply exquisite fragrant ointments to the empty spaces within the boundary of that maṇḍala. Outside the outer maṇḍala, one should apply fine, dense fragrant ointments in a circle with a width of either one or two cubits."
"Furthermore, for the sake of verifying all visions, one should respectively place the seals (mudrās) of one's own mantras.

If the master of the maṇḍala possesses great majestic power and desires to cause his disciples to ultimately abide in the state of a Tathāgata, he should certainly transcribe the mantras of Vajradhātu Mahāsattva and the others, placing each in its respective position."
These are the seals of one’s own speech, all arising from the gateway of the Vajradhātu; they possess great power in accordance with their respective self-activities (*svakarma*).
To explain them in sequence, this secret mantra is recited:
"The first..."
Vajradhātu; second, Akṣobhya; third, Ratnasambhava; fourth.
5. *Rucisavara āraṃ* (twice);
6. *amoghasiddhi*; 7. *vajrasattva*.
8. Vajrāraṅga; 9. Vajrasādhuka; 10. [Vajrāveśa].
11. Vajrāratna 12. Vajratīkṣṇa 13. Vajretiṣya (Vajragītā)
14. Vajrahāsa; 15. Vajradharma; 16. Vajratejas.
17. Vajrakheto 18. Vajrapāśa 19. Vajrakarma
Vajrāraghasa (20); Vajrayakṣa (21); Vajrasandi (22).
Sattvavajre (23), Ratnavajre (24), Dharmavajre (25).
Karmavajre (26), Vajrarāśi (27), Vajramale (28).
Vajranīti (29) Vajranṛtti (30) Vajraduvi (31)
32. Vajrapuṣkariṇī 33. Vajraruci 34. Vajrakānti
35. Vajra-kuśāṅkha (Vajra-kuśaṅkha) 36. Vajrapadma hūṃ 37. Vajrasphoṭa vaṃ

Vajravisahara. Regarding Maitreya and all other bodhisattvas, one should simply extract only the single letter *A*, its color being like snow, or like the halo of the moon, or like the color of a *dūrvā* flower;
or else, at those respective positions, one may simply extract the syllable of Vajrasattva or their individual names.

"Of the sixteen great bodhisattvas, first paint Maitreya; next, Amoghadarśin; next, Sarvaduḥkhapraśamanakara; then, Sarvakṛṣṇāndhakāravidhamanasukha; next, Gandhahastin; then, Śūra; next, Gaganagañja; next, Jñānaketu; next, Amitābha; next, Candraprabha; next, Bhadrapāla; next, Roca; next, Vajragarbha; next, Akṣayamati; next, Pratibhānakūṭa; next, Samantabhadra; and next, Mahāprabha. Furthermore, paint all those who are non-retrogressive, those in the various realms of existence, and even the mahāsattvas on the path of saṃsāra who possess great majesty."

“That Vajrācārya should contemplate these [deities], as well as others such as Vairocana and the various devas residing within the outer maṇḍala who dwell in the desire realm and whose inclinations are disciplined and free from afflictions, and the immeasurable bhikṣus such as Śāriputra who have come to attend; he should contemplate them all.”
Furthermore, one should visualize Maheśvara together with his wife, retinue, and assembly of attendants.

One should also visualize the Ākāśadeva, the Nandikeśvara, and the Sārthavāha; the four sisters of the latter, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Śveta, and Mūṣaladhara; as well as the various deities of the planets and their distinct names.

Furthermore, there were various secret-language spirit-kings, worldly garuḍas, and others, headed by Nārada-deva and Brahmā-deva, as well as celestial kings, world-protector devas, and all the hosts of Māra along with their retinues.
Outside the mandala, one should visualize their respective mudrās, or draw their forms, or simply write down their names.

Next, the ritual procedure for the Vajrācārya is explained: having arranged the positions according to the aforementioned sequence, he again abides in yoga according to the dharma, known as the Vajra-hūṃ-kāra, and then expounds this Hūṃ-samādhi method.
"Furthermore, visualize yourself with slightly protruding fangs, smiling with a wrathful face.

Again, visualize pressing Maheśvara with your left foot and Maheśvara’s wife upon her breasts with your right foot. Next, bind the Mahāsamaya mudrā and hold a flower garland. For the sake of the Ācārya’s sovereignty and out of compassion to benefit all sentient beings, you should enter the maṇḍala. Recite the root mantra and offer the flower garland to the Buddhas according to the ritual, whether with body or mind. Circumambulate the maṇḍala once clockwise, then return to your original place. Following the Vajra rite, take the garland again and place it upon the crown of your head; recite the root mantra and bind it into a topknot."

Furthermore, abiding in yoga, one swiftly turns to the right and dwells at the gateway of the yakṣa direction; surpassing and subduing the forms of the world of the three realms, one opens the four vajra gates with the mind and then utters the mudrā for binding and opening the gates.

"Form two vajra-fists and join them together; with the *tarjanī* fingers of the *vajra-pāṇi* hands, support them facing upward, and hook the *aṅguṣṭha* and *madhyamā* fingers of the *prajñā-pāṇi* hands together. With a wrathful intent, extend the *tarjanī* fingers of the *vajra-pāṇi* hands and push them apart. This is the mudrā of the Supreme Opening of the Door."
Furthermore, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, one should open the gates using this secret mantra (*rahasya-mantra*).

The mantra is: *Oṃ vajranartaka samayapraveśaya hūṃ*. Then, abiding in yoga at the various gates, having opened the gate in the direction of the Yakṣas, one next opens the gate in the direction of Yama according to the ritual; thereafter, moving on, one opens the gate in the direction of Śakra; and next, according to the ritual, one opens the gate in the direction of the Nāgas. All other gates should be opened in this manner, opening them by facing toward each respective gate.

"Next, using an exceptionally fine golden vase or perhaps a silver one, fill it with all kinds of jewels and exquisite fragrant medicines mixed with water. Insert fine branches into the vase; adorn its mouth with various fruits and famous flowers; further smear it with ointments, and tie multicolored silken cloths around its neck."
Having performed the various adornments, one should protect [the site] with secret mantras while maintaining single-minded concentration, placing a flask at each of its primary positions.

If these cannot be prepared, place a flask at each of its four corners and at the entrance. Arrange incense, flowers, various fruits, and all manner of offerings, and proceed in sequence according to the aforementioned method to request the instructions and empower oneself and others.

Having performed this, one should immediately form the seal of the invitation assembly and utter one's own name, entreating all Tathāgatas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas to deign to descend and attend,
chanting this verse three times: "May you come from among all realms of existence,
The sole, solid, and secret one, Who is able to subdue the violent and evil Māras, And directly realize the boundless absence of self-nature."
"I now summon you according to the teachings; may you gather like clouds and oceans. Next, perform the ritual for the mudrā of the Cloud-Gathering Assembly:
having formed the firm *sattvavajra* mudrā, bend the forefinger (*tarjanī*) toward the side of the ring finger (*anāmikā*), slightly curved and separated from it in the shape of a hook.

Having performed that vajra-mudrā, he crosses his arms so that the left hand is inside and the right hand is outside, embracing his chest; then, with both hands, he snaps his fingers several times to summon all Tathāgatas, causing them to assemble like clouds, and recites this secret mantra:

"Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ. From the syllable *jaḥ*, the Great Body Bodhisattva named Vajrameghasaṃcaya arises. One should visualize him in the midst of space, holding a vajra and a *gaṇḍī* bell in his left and right hands respectively, striking them to produce a sound that fills the entirety of space.

"At that time, as soon as this skillful means was issued, all the Tathāgatas and their assemblies of Bodhisattvas from worlds as numerous as the atoms of all directions—aroused by the skillful means of the vajra-finger-snap—gathered like a cloud-ocean pervading all worlds and stood before the masters of the recitation-gate who practice the Bodhisattva path. They were summoned with the vajra-hook, led in with the vajra-noose, bound with the vajra-chain, and made to rejoice with the vajra-bell."
"Next, as previously described, one should visualize each of the seats and sit down with composure.
Then, one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra as previously described and offer argha water."
Next, one should practice the Great Seal of Vajrasattva and swiftly recite the supreme one hundred and eight names once:
"I now pay homage to all Tathāgatas, Samantabhadra, the foremost of Vajras, Vajrasattva, and the Mahāvajrasattva who wields the vajra."
I now pay homage to the Tathāgata Amogharāja, the Supreme Vajrarāja of Wondrous Enlightenment, the Vajra Hook, and the Vajra Summoner.
I now pay homage to the Subduer, the Vanquisher of Māra and all desires, Vajrarāga, Mahāsukha, the Vajra Bow, the Vajra Arrow, and the Mahāvajra.
I now pay homage to Vajrasādhu, Vajrarati, Mahāpramodyarāja, Varasattva, Vajramukha, and Vajrahāsa.
I now pay homage to Vajraratna, Suvajra, Arthavajra, Vajragagana, Mahāmaṇi, Gaganagañja, Vajrasamṛddhi, and Vajragarbha.
I now pay homage to Vajratejas, Vajrasūryavara-prabha, Mahārcivajraprabha, and Mahātejavajraprabha.
I now pay homage to Vajradhvaja, Vajraprabha who brings great benefit to sentient beings, Mahāvajra Ratnaketu who brings great joy, and Vajraratnayaṣṭi.
I now pay homage to Vajra-laughter, Vajra-smile, Mahā-laughter, Vajra-love that gives rise to joy through great wonder, and Vajra-joy.
I now pay homage to Vajradharma, Sattvavara, Vajrapadma, the well-purified Avalokiteśvara, Vajrasudṛṣṭi, and Vajranetra.
I now pay homage to Vajratīkṣṇa, Mahāyāna, Mahāśastra Mañjuśrī, Vajragarbha, Vajragambhīra, and Vajrabodhi.
I now pay homage to the Great Vajracakra, the Vajra of the Principle, the Great Cause, the Solid and Sublime Wheel-Turning Vajra, who arises from the Vajra-maṇḍala.
I now pay homage to the Vajra Speech, the Vajra Recitation that bestows siddhi beyond words, the Supreme Vajra Siddhi, and the Vajra Utterance.
I now pay homage to Vajraviśva, Vajrakarma, Vajrasūkṣmajñāna who pervades all places, Vajramahāviśāla, and Vajrāmogha.
I now pay homage to Vajrapāla, the Great Fearless One; to the Great Armor of Vajra, the Most Firm and Unassailable; to the Foremost in Diligence; and to Vajravīrya.
I now pay homage to the Vajra Yakṣa of Great Expedient Means, the Vajra Fangs most terrifying, the Vajra Supreme Subduer of Māras, and the Vajra Fierce One.
I now pay homage to Vajraguhyājñāsudṛṣṭasiddhi, Vajravāśīsuviśodhana, Vajramuṣṭisusamayasuvikrāmin, and Vajramuṣṭi.
"At that time, because they had gathered like clouds, all Tathāgatas were filled with joy and attained firmness.
Furthermore, Vajrasattva himself became their kinsman and friend, capable of accomplishing all matters."

Next, with the supreme mudrā of Mahākarmā, one should visualize a lotus flower appearing within the flask, endowed with exquisite color and fragrance; then, according to the sequence of yoga practice, one should cause [the deity] to sit upon it in accordance with the pure positions.
"Having formed the Vajra-bond mudrā, divide it into two with a concentrated mind; all subsequent mudrās should follow this same principle.

With the vajra-finger of the left hand (the *śamatha* wing), one should grasp [it] with the right hand (the *vipaśyanā* wing); this is called the Supreme Bodhi Mudrā, which can bestow the bodhi of the Buddhas."

"Having bound this Great Seal (Mahāmudrā), one should visualize the Honored One Vairocana seated in the center of the mandala, sitting in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka). He possesses great majestic power; his color is like that of a white goose, and his form is like the pure moon. All his marks and signs (lakṣaṇa-vyañjana) are perfectly complete. His head is adorned with a jeweled crown, and his hair hangs down decorated with silken ribbons. Light and exquisite celestial garments encircle his waist, while fine upper robes are draped over him. With all vidyā-mantras as his very body, he is able to perform immeasurable supernatural transformations, and constantly fills the realm of birth and death (saṃsāra) with the vajra-wheel of samādhi."
Having prepared the Great Wheel Seal (Mahācakra-mudrā) and completed the placement of its marks, one should contemplate the World-Honored One in this manner;
thus, one will immediately accomplish all *karmas*. Then, he spoke these secret words:

"Oṃ Vajra-dhātu vaṃ. Next, one should further visualize all the Sugatas with white and yellow lotuses—Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, Avalokiteśvara, and Amoghasiddhi—the Great Sages of various exquisite and unfailing colors.
Having performed this contemplation, one attains immeasurable fruits; one should then sequentially establish the fundamental mudrās according to the Dharma.
The *Akṣobhya* is named the "Earth-Touching Mudrā," for which the secret mantra is:
*Oṃ Akṣobhya Hūṃ*. The *Ratnasambhava* is named the "Bestowing of Wishes Mudrā," for which the secret mantra is:
"Oṃ arthasiddhisambhava tra. [This is] the mudrā of the Samādhi of the Victorious Excellence of Amitāyus;
recite this mantra: "Oṃ lu-ke śvāra-rāja-hrīḥ. [This is] the mudrā of Amoghasiddhi Bestowing Fearlessness;
the mantra is: "Oṃ amoghasiddhe 'ḥ. Furthermore, bind the mudrās of Vajrasattva and the others.
Regarding the clarification of the ritual procedures: having visualized each [gesture] in its proper sequence, one establishes it.

With a majestic and spirited demeanor, one performs two shaking motions; that is to say, one forms two vajra-fists, places the thumbs at the heart, and contemplates the thumbs as being in the posture of brandishing a *vajra*.
Recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasattva āḥ. Having crossed the elbows with the two [hands] held upright like hooks, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra raṅ. Having formed the two [hands] as if releasing an arrow, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrārogya hoḥ. Again, using the two vajras at the heart, perform the "Excellent" (Sādhu) mudrā, snap the fingers, and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasādhu saḥ. Again, placing the two [vajras] upon the forehead, perform the consecration (abhiṣeka), and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrārotra oṃ. Again, placing the two vajras at the heart, rotate them like the solar disc and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-ti-raṅgaḥ. Again, placing the two upright [fingers] of the right elbow upon the left fist to form a banner, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-ketu-tālaṃ. Then, place the finger-mudrās of those same two fists at the mouth and scatter them upward with both hands, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-ha-saha. Visualize the left hand as a *kumuda* flower and split open the petals of the right hand, while reciting this mantra:

"Oṃ vajradharmahri. Again, place the left hand upon the heart as if it were the obstacle of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*), and with the right hand forming a sword, visualize its destruction while reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajratejas taṃ. Again, extend both arms before you and rotate them like a wheel, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrayodhamaha. Again, raise both hands from the mouth, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-pāśa ālaṃ. Again, performing the Vajra Dance with the two hands entwined, touching the two breasts and the two cheeks, and placing them upon the crown of the head, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-karma khaṅ. Again, using the two hands to encircle the waist from the chest as if donning armor, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-argha haṃ. Again, extending the two *tarjanī* fingers and the *jyeṣṭhā*, *madhyamā*, and *anāmikā* fingers like tusks and placing them at both sides of the mouth, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra yakṣa hūṃ. Again, join the two fists together and press them, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra muṣṭi vaṃ. Again, with the two little fingers bowed down, manifesting respect through the vajra-mind, recite this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra rāśe huḥ. Again, using the ritual for binding a garland, bind it upon the head, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra māle traṭ. Again, using two [fingers], place them at the heart; as if emitting [the syllables] from the mouth, recite while extending the arms downward, pronouncing this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra nīrati. Again, using two [fingers], perform the dance ritual and place them upon the crown of the head, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra nṛtye kṛta. Again, using two [fingers], cover the hands with palms open and press them downward, reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajra dhūpe āḥ. Again, open both palms facing upward and raise them; recite this mantra: "Oṃ vajra puṣpe oṃ.
Again, bring the two hands together and press them firmly to form the lamp mudrā; recite this mantra: "Oṃ vajra āloke hūṃ.
Again, place the two hands at the heart and rub the chest, then draw them outward and separate them to form the unguent mudrā; recite this mantra:

"Oṃ vajra-gaṇḍe raḥ. Again, using the two [thumbs] with palms facing away, hook the *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers, extend the *ati-prajñā* fingers like needles, and curve the *upāya* fingers to form hooks;
recite this mantra: "Oṃ vajra-kuśalaṃ reka. Again, using the two [thumbs] as before with palms facing away, hook them and cross the *ati-prajñā* fingers, supporting them together to form a noose;
recite this mantra: "Oṃ vajra-pāśa hūṃ hūṃ. Again, using the two *ati-prajñā* fingers, hook them together to form a chain; recite this mantra:

"Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ. Again, using the two hands with the *tarjanī* and *madhyamā* fingers turned away from each other, hook them together; then, with the *pradeśinī* fingers of the first division, cross them to form a bell while reciting this secret mantra:
"Oṃ vajravicaya hoḥ. Next, perform the mudrās of the four families of Akṣobhya, and further perform the mudrās of the four *pāramitās* and so forth, applying them in their proper sequence.

Furthermore, outside the maṇḍala, using the *yǎngzhǐ* (upward-stopping) feather-fist mudrā, one should place the Mahāsattva and all other sattvas as appropriate; touching the ground and performing the visualization, they are thus installed.

"Next, the accomplishment of all mudrās is explained: one should visualize vajras at the four sides within one's own heart, and then, according to the ritual procedure, bind the various karma-mudrās."
Next, praise the merits of the aforementioned mudrās:
by binding the Great Wisdom Fist Mudrā, one is able to enter the Buddha-wisdom;
by binding the Akṣobhya Earth-Touching Mudrā, one attains an unshakable mind.
By binding the Ratnasambhava mudrā, one is able to gather and benefit others;
by binding the Samādhi mudrā, one is able to maintain the samādhi of the Buddha;
by binding the Supreme Mudrā for Dispelling Fear, one is able to swiftly bestow fearlessness upon sentient beings.
Furthermore, by binding the mental disposition of the Vajra Fist mudrā, one easily becomes a Vajrasattva;
by binding the Vajra Hook, one is able to swiftly summon all Tathāgatas;
and by binding the Vajra Passion mudrā, even if she be a Vajra consort, one is able to become impassioned with her.
By binding the Vajra-joy mudrā, all the most excellent ones praise them, saying "Excellent!";
by binding the Great Vajra-jewel mudrā, the Teachers of Gods and Humans confer empowerment upon them;
by binding the Vajra-sun mudrā, they attain equality with the Vajra-sun.
By binding the Vajradhvaja-mudrā, one is able to pour down a rain of various jewels;
by binding the Vajrasmita-mudrā, one swiftly attains the same smile as all Buddhas;
by binding the Vajrapuṣpa-mudrā, one is able to perceive the Vajra-dharma.
By binding the Vajragarbha-sword mudrā, one is able to sever all suffering;
by binding the Vajracakra mudrā, one is able to turn the wheel of Dharma taught by all Tathāgatas;
by binding the Vajrabhāṣa mudrā, one is able to attain the accomplishment of recitation.
By binding the Vajra-karma mudrā, one is able to accord with the activities of all Tathāgatas;
by binding the Vajra-varma mudrā, one attains the nature of vajra-solidity;
by binding the Vajra-daṃṣṭra mudrā, even a vajra can be crushed to pieces.
By binding the Vajra-fist mudrā, one is able to obtain all mudrās and attain siddhi;
by binding the Vajra-joy-play delightful mudrā, one constantly experiences all forms of joy;
by binding the Vajra-garland mudrā, one obtains a beautiful and exquisite countenance.
By binding the vajra song mudrā, one obtains pure and wondrous speech;
by binding the vajra dance mudrā and the offering mudrā, one attains the subjugation of all beings;
by binding the vajra incense mudrā, one obtains a pleasing environment.
By binding the vajra-flower mudrā, one obtains all manner of adornments;
by binding the vajra-lamp offering mudrā, one attains great majestic radiance;
by binding the vajra-unguent mudrā, one acquires exquisite fragrance.
By forming the vajra-aṅkuśa mudrā, one is able to summon;
by forming the vajra-pāśa mudrā, one is able to lead [the deity] in;
