by forming the vajra-sphoṭa mudrā, one is able to bind and detain them.
By means of binding the vajra-ghaṇṭā mudrā, one is able to generate joy.
Furthermore, the wisdom of binding the vajra-samaya mudrā of all Tathāgatas is explained.

When forming the mudrās of the samaya and so forth, one must first visualize within one’s own heart the great and most excellent five-pronged vajra born from the samādhi of all Tathāgatas. Then, joining the two hands, first interlace the fingers and observe the thumbs pressing upon the thumbs; this is called the Vajra-pañjali (Vajra-clasp).
Bringing the tips of all the mudrās together so that they interlock, this is called the Vajrabandha seal; all samaya seals without exception arise from this supreme Vajrabandha.
"I shall now explain the methods for the various samaya-mudrās in their proper sequence:

Having formed the vajra-bond (vajrabandha), extend the two middle fingers (tarjanī and anāmikā) and tuck their bases; interlock them to form a blade, and bend the two index fingers (tarjanī) alongside the blade. This is the Vairocana-Vajradhātu-Īśvara-mudrā."
The secret mantra says:

*Oṃ vajra-tuṣya-śvā-hrī-vārīṇi hūṃ*. Next, having performed the original binding mudrā, join and extend the two fingers of the patience and vow [mudrās] upright to form a stalk; this is called the Samaya-mudrā of Buddha Akṣobhya.
The secret mantra is:

*Oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ*. Having bound the mudrā according to the original vow, bend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhāna* (little finger) fingers so that their first joints touch; with the faces of the *jñāna* (middle) and *samādhi* (index) fingers touching, form the jewel. This is called the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Ratnasaṃbhava.
The secret mantra is:

*Oṃ aratnavañjari hūṃ*. Having performed the original binding mudrā, bend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhāna* (little finger) fingers so that they touch each other like a flower; this is called the Samaya-mudrā of Amitābha Buddha.
The secret mantra is:

Oṃ vajradharme hūṃ. Having formed the original binding mudrā, bend the ring and little fingers into the palms, and extend the thumbs, middle, and wisdom fingers like needles; this is called the Samaya-mudrā of Amoghasiddhi Buddha.
The secret mantra is: Oṃ vajrakarmavajriṇi hūṃ.

Next, the mudrās of Vajrasattva and others are explained: having formed the vajra-bind (vajrabandha) mudrā, visualize the two palms as moon discs; join and extend the two thumbs (kṣānti) and two ring fingers (praṇidhi), while keeping the two index fingers (dāna) and two middle fingers (prajñā) upright and not joined, forming the shape of a five-pronged vajra. This is called the Sattvavajra mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

*Oṃ samayasattva*. Having performed the original binding mudrā, bend the forefinger to form a hook; with the tip of the index finger at a distance of two or three *aṅgulas*, this is called the Samaya-mudrā of the Mahāsattva Amogharāja.
The secret mantra is:
*Oṃ ānaya sattva*. Having performed the original binding mudrā, bend the fingers of the two hands so that they cross at their midpoints; this is called the *Māra-mahābodhisattva-samaya-mudrā*.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ āhu suka. Having performed the original binding mudrā, one should pinch the *jñāna-samādhi-pāṇi* with the *vīrya-bala-pāṇi*, snapping the fingers for each as a sign of "well done" (*sādhu*). This is called the Vajra-leaping Sattva Samaya Mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ sādhu sādhu. As for the original *baddhasthita-jñāna-samādhi-mudrā*: extend the arms forward and bend them at the elbows, with the palms facing each other; this is called the *samaya-mudrā* of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
The secret mantra says: “Oṃ sumahā-tva.
As in the original, extend the *tana* [fingers] of the binding; open the palms—this is called the Samaya-mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajraprabha.
The secret mantra says:
*Oṃ rumbu-ni-yuta*. As in the original binding, join the thumbs and ring fingers together; this is called the Vajra Banner and is also known as the Bodhisattva Samaya Mudrā of the Vajra Support.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ arita pratyūha. Then, place the aforementioned mudrā on both cheeks at the position of the smile; turn the hands over to release it and raise them apart. This is called the Vajrapriya Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

*Oṃ hā hā hā hā hūṃ ha*. As for the mudrā: bind it as in the original, extend the wisdom and concentration fingers upright, and bend the strength and progress fingers so their tips touch one another; this is called the Samaya-mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajranetra.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ sarvakāli. As in the original binding, extend the fingers of the *kṣānti* (patience) and *praṇidhāna* (vow) mudrās, bend their initial segments, and join them like the blades of swords; this is called the Vajrakhaḍga Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ nukha che na. As for the mudrā: join the *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers together as they were originally bound; this is called the Vajracakra Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ bhaḥ dhā puṭi. As in the original binding, extend the wisdom and concentration fingers outward from the mouth; this is called the Vajravāc Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

*Oṃ pratisaṃbodha*. As in the original binding, one presses the *dāna-pāramitā* with the *jñāna-samādhi-pāramitā* to form the *karmavajra*; this is called the *samaya-mudrā* of the Bodhisattva Viśvakarman.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ supoṣita va. As in the original, extend the fingers of the right hand upward and place them upon the heart; this is called the Samaya-mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vīra.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ dīne baya dha va. [As in the original, with *va* curved; the *jiṇila* [curved] and *daluò* [open] fingers represent the *pāramitās* of power and wisdom as the fangs. This is called the Vajrayakṣa Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says: "Oṃ śatru-pakṣa.

As for the original binding: with the wisdom and concentration fingers (the ring fingers), grasp the space between the thumb and the wisdom finger (the little finger); bend the effort finger (the middle finger) over the back of the wisdom and concentration fingers. This is called the Vajramuṣṭi Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ sarvasiddhi. Having bound it as in the original and placed it at the heart, one extends the wisdom and concentration fingers; this is named the Vajra-Love, the mudrā of the Samaya of the Secret Offering Goddess of Playful Amusement.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ mahāratne. As in the original binding, extend both arms long to form a garland; this is called the Vajramālā-devī Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ ru paśve. Form the vajra-añjali mudrā, draw it forth from the mouth, and extend the arms downward; this is called the Vajragīta-devatā-samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:

“Oṃ śūnyatā-svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ śūnyatā-svabhāva-śuddho ’ham. Then, having opened the previous mudrā and performed a circling motion like a dance, one places the palms together upon the crown of the head; this is called the Vajra Dance Offering Deva Samaya Mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sarvapuṣpe. As in the original binding, cover the palms of both hands and press them downward; this is called the Samaya-mudrā for the offering of incense to the devas.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ praharaṇi. As in the original binding, turn both palms upward and raise them; this is called the *samaya-mudrā* of the Flower-Offering Deva.
The secret mantra is:
Oṃ phala gaḥ. As for the original binding mudrā, extend the wisdom and concentration fingers; this is called the Samaya Mudrā of the Deity of Lamp Offering.
The secret mantra says:

"Oṃ sudhāraṅkari. As in the original binding, open the palms and rub them against the chest; then, spreading them apart toward the outside, this is called the Samaya-mudrā for making the offering of scented unguent to the devas.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sugata nī. As for the original binding, bend the fingers of the grasping hand into the shape of a hook; this is called the Vajrāṅkuśa Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ āye raṅkha. Having bound it as before and fixed it crosswise, press it down with the *prajñāpāramitā*; with the head entering the palm, this is called the Vajrapāśa Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ. As for the original binding, one hooks and pierces [the fingers] with the *dāna-pāramitā* and *prajñā-pāramitā*; this is called the Vajra-Chain Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra is:
Oṃ kheḥ sphuṭa phaṭ. As in the original binding, with the fingers of wisdom and concentration joined together inside the palms, this is called the Vajrāveśa Bodhisattva Samaya-mudrā.
The secret mantra is:
"Oṃ khaṇḍa ā ā. Next, the merits of the aforementioned samaya-mudrās are explained:
by means of the Buddha-anusmṛti mudrā, one is able to swiftly realize bodhi.
By means of the Sattva-vajra mudrā, one is able to become the sovereign lord of all mudrās;
by means of the Ratna-vajra mudrā, one attains the mastery of all jewels;
by means of the Dharma-vajra mudrā, one attains the treasury of the Buddha-dharma.
By means of the Karma-vajra mudrā, one is able to perform all activities;
by means of the Sattva mudrā, one attains the body of Vajrasattva;
and by means of the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā, one is able to summon all the Vajradharas.
By means of the Vajra-rāga-mudrā, one is able to delight in all Buddha-dharmas;
by means of the Vajra-sādhu-mudrā, one is able to cause all Buddhas to rejoice;
by means of the Ratna-mudrā, one attains the stage of Buddha-abhiṣeka.
By means of the Vajratejas mudrā, one attains vajra splendor;
by means of the Vajradhvaja mudrā, one is able to grant the fulfillment of all wishes;
by means of the Vajrahāsa mudrā, one is able to laugh together with all Buddhas.
By means of the Vajradharma mudrā, one is able to uphold the vajra-dharma;
by means of the Vajratīkṣṇa mudrā, one attains the supreme wisdom of the Buddha;
by means of the Vajracakra mudrā, one is able to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
By means of the Vajra Speech mudrā, one attains the siddhi of the Buddha’s speech;
by means of the Vajra Action mudrā, one swiftly attains the supreme accomplishment;
and by means of the Vajra Armor mudrā, one becomes a vajra body.
By means of the Vajrayakṣa mudrā, one becomes equal to a Vajrayakṣa;
by means of the Vajramuṣṭi mudrā, one achieves all mudrās;
and by means of the Vajralāsyā mudrā, one attains great bliss.
By means of the Vajramālā mudrā, one receives the Buddha’s empowerment;
by means of the Vajragīta mudrā, one obtains the Dharma of the Buddha’s hymns of praise;
and by means of the Vajranṛtya mudrā, one receives the Buddha’s protection and bestowal of offerings.
By means of the Vajra Incense Mudrā, one is able to bring glory and purity to all realms;
by means of the Vajra Flower Mudrā, one causes the world to become compliant;
by means of the Vajra Light Mudrā, one attains the five eyes of a Buddha.
By means of the Vajra-unguent mudrā, one can eliminate all suffering and calamity;
by means of the Vajra-sarvamudrādhipati mudrā, one can summon and attract all;
by means of the Vajra-pāśa mudrā, one can lead all [beings] within.
By means of the Vajra-Chain mudrā, one is able to bind and restrain all;
by means of the Vajra-Summoning mudrā, one is able to accomplish the gathering and inclusion of all.

Next, one should perform offerings to all Tathāgatas using the sixteen great offering mudrās. Having formed the Vajra-Bond, perform them in their respective locations according to the sequence: join the Vajra-Bond from the heart, then the left flank, the right flank, and the back; next, the forehead, the mouth, the two ears, the nape of the neck, the right shoulder, and the waist. Once the circuit is complete, place it back upon the heart.
"Now, I shall explain in sequence the secret mantras for the sixteen great offerings.
The secret mantra for the heart is as follows: *Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvadharmātman-niryātaya pūjāṃ sāṃpūrṇa-karma-bhaṅgali āḥ*. The commentary states:”
"I offer my entire body to all Tathāgatas, making universal offerings and performing all manner of activities.
The mantra for the *vāmapārśva-mudrā* (left-side posture) is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvadharma-nirjāta-prabharaṇa-karmakari*. The commentary states:
"I offer my entire body to all Tathāgatas and universally present it as an offering.
The mantra for the Supreme Karmic Right-Lateral Seal is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvadharmadeyātman-anurāgaṇa-kārya-prayoga-spharaṇa-karmabandha hūṃ haḥ*. The commentary states:
Having offered one’s entire body to all Tathāgatas, one universally makes offerings to the *karma* bow and arrow.
The secret mantra of the "Waohou" (*yāohòu*) mudrā is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata-sarvadharmadeya-tantra-sādhu-kāra-svāhā-bhujaḥ spharaṇa-karmadṛśo-sthita-sampraharṣa-saṃ*. The commentary states:
To all Tathāgatas, one offers oneself with the entire body, universally making offerings with the sound of "Excellent!
(*sādhu*) for the sake of joyful activities.
The secret mantra of the *mudrā* on the forehead is: *Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatakāyavilokite hradani pū vajramaye oṃ*. The commentary states:
"I now pay homage to all the jewels that have been consecrated upon the bodies of all Tathāgatas.
[Visualize] the *vajra-maṇi* rotating upon the heart like the orb of the sun;
the mantra is: *Oṃ namas sarvatathāgata-sūrye-bhāsa-vajra-tejini-jvala-hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"I now pay homage to all Tathāgatas, Vajrasūrya, and the rest.
Placing the seal of blazing majesty upon the crown of the head, extend both arms long and recite this mantra:
"Oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatāśeṣapralambanacintāmaṇivajraratnākara hūṃ traṃ. The commentary states:
I now pay homage to all Tathāgatas, who fulfill all that is sought through their wish-fulfilling jewels.
Regarding the "Supreme Vajra Banner" at the place of the smile upon the mouth, when loosening the vajra-bond, the secret mantra for the method of releasing the mudrā is as follows:
Oṃ namo sarvatathāgatebhyo mahāpūritatindri-pramuditāyākāṅkṣa-vajrahāsasvāhā. The commentary states:
Homage to all Tathāgatas who bring forth joy.
The secret mantra of the Vajra-Laughter Face is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmatāvajrasamatāviśuddhe saṃstute mahādharmakīrti*. The commentary states:
With the *samādhi* of the Vajra-dharmatā of all Tathāgatas, he praised the Great Sound of Dharma (*mahā-dharmasvara*).
The secret mantra for the left ear is as follows:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgataprajñāpāramitā-avine-nihāri-stunumim praśaṃsa mahākuśanuni me idam.* The commentary states:
One should praise with a great voice using the words issued from the *prajñāpāramitā* of all Tathāgatas.
The secret mantra for the right ear is as follows:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrākṣaraparivartani sarvasutrāntāñjucchatānaye saddharmamudraṇe sarvamaṇḍale hūṃ.* The commentary states:
With the wheel of syllables of all Tathāgatas as its foremost feature, the principles of the various mudrās and sūtras praise all sites of enlightenment (*maṇḍala*).
The secret mantra following the "Crown" (*uṣṇīṣa*) is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgata-santarpaṇa-mantrodbhava-saṃgīti-vigāyana-gāyanastotranamaḥ vajra-paricaya*. The commentary states:
I now sing and praise the vajra speech through the secret words of all Tathāgatas.
The secret word for the crown of the head is: Oṃ sarvatathāgata.

*Dūpa* means incense; *megha* means clouds; *samudra* means oceans; *spharaṇa* means pervading everywhere. [This is] for the sake of the ritual activity (*karmaprasarā*) of making offerings. *Kāra kāra*. The Commentary says:
This refers to the ritual activity of universally making offerings with oceans of clouds of incense from all Tathāgatas.
The secret mantra for the right shoulder is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpābhyaḥ pravara-spharaṇa-prayoga-karma kṛiṃ kṛiṃ*. The commentary states:
This is because one performs the activity of universally making offerings with clouds of various wondrous flowers of all the Tathāgatas.
The secret mantra for the right knee is:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatārūpaka-jvala-spharaṇapūrṇakarmabala-bala*. The commentary states:
"One should universally make offerings with the blazing light of all Tathāgatas in order to perform the *karma*.
Having performed it as described above, one places [the mantra] upon the heart;
the secret mantra is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgata-gandha-vilepana-samudra-spharaṇa-prayoga-kṛme kṛme*. The commentary says:
Because one performs activities by universally making offerings with oceans of clouds of unguents of all Tathāgatas.

"Having thus performed what is to be done with these sixteen great offering mudrās, one should immediately bind the Great Seal of the Flower Mudrā as described above, survey the ten directions, and speak these words:
'I now entreat all Buddhas:'"
"May those who have not yet turned the wheel of Dharma turn the wheel of Dharma;
may those who wish to enter parinirvāṇa remain forever in the world and not pass into parinirvāṇa.
He further thought:

"I now offer this Jambudvīpa, as well as all flowers from the heavens and earth, and those produced by the minds of humans and devas throughout the worlds of the ten directions; I offer them all to all the Mahābodhisattvas of the ten directions, to the retinues dwelling in all their families, and to all the deities of the mantras and mudrās, so that I may perform the work of making offerings to all the Tathāgatas."
Recite the secret mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpameghapracārasamudra spharaṇasamaye hūṃ phaṭ*. The Commentary states:
"One universally makes offerings with oceans of flower-clouds of all the Tathāgatas."
"Furthermore, form the mudrā for burning incense and contemplate thus:

'I now offer all the various types of incense belonging to humans and devas—namely, natural incense, blended incense, and transformed incense, such as that produced by camphor and other flowers through fumigation or soaking—to serve as an offering for the *karma* of all Tathāgatas.'"
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata dhūpa-saugandhika-pramukha-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary states:
One should universally make offerings with oceans of incense clouds of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, having bound the ointment mudrā, one should form this thought:
"For the sake of making offerings to the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, I now present these various types of incense—the natural incenses of humans and devas, blended incenses, and transformed incenses."
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-gandha-puṣpa-maṅgala-samudra-spharaṇa."
*Samaye hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"One universally makes offerings with clouds and oceans of ointments from all the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, having formed the lamp mudrā, one should contemplate as follows:

"Whatever essential nature belongs to humans and devas, and whatever self-arisen, diverse radiance—such as precious jewels—that delights the mind, I now offer this for the sake of performing services in offering to all Tathāgatas."
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-nirbhāsa-prabhāsana-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary states:
"One universally makes offerings with clouds and oceans of lamps of all the Tathāgatas."
"Having formed the Vajraratna mudrā, one should form this thought:

'Whatever kinds of jewels exist upon all the jewel-mountains in this world and in other worlds, as well as those within the earth and the oceans—all these I now offer for the sake of making offerings to the activity (karma) of all Tathāgatas.'"
The secret mantra says:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgataguṇasamudrasamavasaraṇa-prabhāsvara-samantāloke hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"One universally makes offerings with clouds and oceans of precious ornaments of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣa*) of all Tathāgatas."
Having formed the seal of playful sport, one reflects thus:
"I now offer all the various implements for play, jesting, and music possessed by humans and devas, for the sake of the activities of making offerings to all Tathāgatas."
The secret mantra says:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata hāsyalalita-kṛtiharṣitaskandhānuttarapūjā-samudra-spharaṇasamaye hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"One makes offerings pervasively with an ocean of clouds of supreme joy and play, which are the playful amusements of all Tathāgatas."
The Vajraśekhara Yoga Sūtra: A Brief Extraction of the Recitation Ritual, Scroll Three.
The Vajraśekhara Yoga Sūtra: A Brief Extraction of the Recitation Ritual, Scroll Four.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty:
"Having bound the *sattvavajra-mudrā*, one should reflect thus:

'Just as the kings, elders, and householders of the western continent [Aparagoyānī] adorn the various *kalpavṛkṣa* (wish-fulfilling trees) with diverse flowers, perfumes, and necklaces, and offer them to all; and just as those *kalpavṛkṣas* are able to provide various garments and articles for adorning the body—all for the sake of performing services in offering to all Tathāgatas—I now present these offerings. "
The secret mantra says:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatānuttaradharmadhātupadmasamādhipadmabhajanabhuñjana-saṃvartana-megha-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ*. The commentary states:
By means of the cultivation of the samādhi of all Tathāgatas, which is like the supreme vajra, one universally makes offerings of sublime food, drink, and clothing, as vast as an ocean of clouds.
"Having performed the *vajra-mudrā* of the *karmasaṃbandha*, one should reflect:
'In order that all Tathāgatas within the treasury of space may be supported, I shall imagine that before each and every Buddha there is my own self, personally attending and serving them.'"
He recites the secret mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇītejodhātu-maṅgala-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"One offers oneself as a tribute to the ocean-like clouds of all Tathāgatas, making offerings to them all universally."
"Having formed the Dharma-vajra mudrā, one should contemplate thus:
'This body of mine is now identical to the bodies of all bodhisattvas, without any difference.'"
Furthermore, one should observe that the true nature of all phenomena is equal and without distinction.
Having performed this contemplation, recite the secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatajñānādhyeṣaṇasamudrānugate samayehūṃ. The commentary states:
One should offer clouds and oceans of the hearts of all Tathāgatas as universal offerings.
Having formed the Jewel Banner Mudrā, one should further contemplate:

"All sentient beings within the entirety of saṃsāra are entangled in suffering and affliction; generating deep compassion for them, I now resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in order to rescue and protect them."
Therefore, those who have not yet crossed over, I shall cause them to cross;
those who have not yet been comforted, I shall cause them to be comforted;
and those who have not yet attained nirvāṇa, I shall cause them to attain nirvāṇa.
"And may there fall rains of various jewels, so that whatever they seek shall all be fulfilled.
Having reflected thus, he recited this secret mantra:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatamahāvajrotpabhamadāparimitapūjāmoghasamudraspharaṇasamaye hūṃ. The Commentary says:
One should universally make offerings with clouds and oceans of the *dānapāramitā* born from the great vajra of all Tathāgatas.
Having formed the fragrance-body mudrā, one should contemplate thus:
"May all sentient beings be forever removed from all unwholesome aspirations of body, speech, and mind, and may they achieve all wholesome dharmas."
Having formed this thought, he recited this secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatānuttaramahābodhy-ārgha-kusuma-pāramitā-puṣpāṅgī-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The Commentary says:
This means that one universally makes offerings with an ocean-like cloud of the excellent precepts born of the unsurpassed bodhi of all Tathāgatas.
"Having bound the earth-touching mudrā, one further forms this thought:

'May all sentient beings accomplish a mind of loving-kindness, free from mutual affliction and harm; may they be liberated from all fears, look upon one another with hearts of joy, adorn their bodies with the various marks and signs of excellence, and accomplish the treasury of all profound dharmas.'"
Having reflected thus, he recited this secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatānuttaramahādharmajālāpratihatavikrāntipāramitā-praśāntaghasmara-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary states:
“By means of the ocean-like clouds of the *pāramitā* of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), which is the supreme awakening to the Great Dharma of all Tathāgatas, one makes universal offerings.”
"Having bound the Vajra-Strife-Victory-Vigor Mudrā, one should reflect thus:
'May all sentient beings cultivate the bodhisattva practices and don the firm armor of vigor.'"
Having formed this thought, he recited this secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-saṃsāra-ha-pratibhaṅga-mahāvīrya-pāramitā-bhūja-miṅga-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary states:
By means of the cloud-ocean of the great *pāramitā* of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) that does not abandon *saṃsāra*, one universally makes offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
"Form the supreme mudrā of the Samādhi-knot and contemplate thus:

'May all sentient beings be able to fully subdue their afflictions (*kleśa*) and secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*), which are their enemies, and may they attain the characteristics of all profound meditative absorptions (*dhyāna-samādhi*)."
Having formed this thought, he recited this secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgatānuttaramahāsaukhyakṣetrapratipādananirmala-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary states:
“By means of the ocean-like clouds of the *dhyāna-pāramitā* of the unsurpassed great bliss-abiding of all Tathāgatas, one makes universal offerings.”
"Having bound the Ratnasambhava mudrā, which bestows the vows of all Tathāgatas upon all sentient beings, one should reflect as follows:

'May all sentient beings achieve mastery in the five fields of knowledge (*pañcavidyāsthāna*); may they universally accomplish all mundane and supramundane wisdom; may they attain true vision; may they obtain the wisdom that exhaustively eliminates the afflictive and cognitive obscurations; and may their minds be adorned with all the Buddha-dharmas, such as eloquence and fearlessness.'"
Having formed this thought, he recited this secret mantra:
“Oṃ sarvatathāgata-anuttara-ajñāna-vāraṇa-vāsana-mardana-mahāprajñāpāramitā-bhūmi-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The commentary says:
One should universally make offerings with clouds and oceans of the Great Wisdom Pāramitā that purify the habitual tendencies of afflictions through the unsurpassed subduing of all Tathāgatas.
Having formed the seal of the supreme Samādhi, one should contemplate:
"The true nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty, signless, and wishless; all phenomena are entirely like this."
Having performed this visualization, one recites this secret mantra:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgata-avahiyamima mahāparipatti-prayogabhṛṅga-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ*. The commentary states:
"By means of this, clouds and oceans of all secret practices are universally offered."
Furthermore, one should reflect:
"May the words and sounds I now utter be heard by all sentient beings.
Having formed this thought, recite this secret mantra:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavāgīśvarīye tantra prajñāsamudra spharaṇasamaye hūṃ. Thereafter, one should perform a song with vajra speech, reciting this verse:
"Because Vajrasattva has taken me into his care, I have become the unsurpassed Vajraratna;
Through the singing of vajra speech, May the supreme vajra activity be accomplished."
Furthermore, one should praise him with adamantine speech in a pure and beautiful tone, reciting this verse:
"Among all the various types of beings in all worlds, You perform Buddha-deeds as numerous as atoms;
The Tathāgata manifests great supernatural transformations, Appearing in various bodies according to what is appropriate."
The peerless, immovable, and eternally firm Dharma, Whose compassionate essence can eliminate the suffering of the world,
Which bestows all the merits of *siddhi*, Is the peerless, equal, powerful, and supreme Dharma.
There is no analogy for it; it is like space. Even a small portion of its merit is boundless.
The supreme siddhi that pervades the realm of sentient beings—unequaled and immeasurable—is entirely capable of being accomplished.
The eternal nature is pure, arising from compassion; Through the fulfillment of aspirational power, he dwells in the world.
Able to bring about boundless benefit and happiness, Great compassion is his essence, eternally and universally illuminating.
The conduct of compassion is unshakable and does not grasp at cessation; wandering to transform beings within the three realms, you bestow *siddhi*.
Having thoroughly mastered all that is immeasurable, though you have already passed into bliss, you manifest wondrous wonders.
Ever-abiding through the three periods of time, with unimpeded power, Supreme refuge beyond surpassing,
able to bestow all samayas— May I swiftly attain the supreme siddhi!
“Having praised him thus, if there are further superior and sublime verses of praise, one may praise him as one pleases.

Regarding the method of chanting: at dawn, one should praise with the *śārdūla* (lion) melody; at midday, with the middle melody; at twilight, with the *bhinnaka* (broken) melody; and at midnight, with the fifth melody.”
If one does not understand it, one should praise it with pure and beautiful sounds and should constantly recite it four times every day—namely, at dawn, midday, dusk, and midnight.
One should hold four kinds of rosaries and perform four types of recitation—those four being: first, vocal recitation;

second, vajra recitation, which is silent recitation with the mouth closed and the tongue moving; third, samādhi recitation, which is mental recitation; and fourth, true recitation, which is practicing according to the meaning of the syllables. By the power of these four types of recitation, one is able to extinguish all karmic obstacles, afflictions, and calamities, and accomplish all meritorious virtues.

Regarding the four types of rosaries: for the Tathāgata family, one uses bodhi seeds; for the Vajra family, vajra seeds; for the Ratna family, precious gems; for the Padma family, lotus seeds; and for the Karma family, they are made from various jewels interspersed together.
If a practitioner is able to practice samādhi and recitation in accordance with yoga, there shall be no limitation of time or number; they should perform it at all times without interruption.
"Next, the method for offering food and drink shall be explained: one should offer various kinds of fragrant and pure food and drink.
If one is unable to provide these, having performed as much as one’s strength allows, one should further bring them to mind, thinking:
'I offer every single kind of supreme and exquisite food and drink found in the world, various rare fruits such as grapes and pomegranates, and all manner of non-seasonal juices.'"
"If you yourself do not obtain [the materials], then those who perform the offerings should cause disciples who clearly understand this dharma to act as described above.

Furthermore, one should offer worship by using ointments, incense, various exquisite flowers, lamps, garlands, and *mallika* flowers; likewise, by mixing various foods, drinks, fruits, and the like with water and placing them in jars and basins, one performs the offering for the sake of giving to the spirits (*bhūta-graha*)."

Furthermore, with banners, streamers, silk canopies, exquisite celestial garments, and other various superior articles of offering, each accompanied by its respective *mantra*—or by adding the *mantra* of the principal deity of the family, which refers here to the speech of the Buddhas of the five families—one should make offerings according to one's capacity.
"If a practitioner seeks the merits of the Tathāgata, when performing offerings with utmost sincerity within the maṇḍala as described above, they shall behold Vajrasattva face to face."
If you do not see [the deity], you should again offer prayers with utmost sincerity.
Depending on what is evoked by the karmic power of the practitioner, once you have seen various Buddhas or Sattvas and so forth, you should immediately offer them that garland.

At that time, the practitioner should rejoice within himself, place the offered garland upon his own crown, append the mantra of his respective family, and bind it upon his head; one should know that such a person will thereby obtain extraordinary and superior merit and retribution.

When the practitioner has finished performing the offerings, they should immediately exit the mandala. Taking beans, fruits, cakes, rice, sesame flour, various flowers, and so forth, they should mix them with water and place them in a vase or basin; then, with a joyful mind, scatter them in the four directions as an offering to the devas, spirits, and their retinues, bestowing them upon each according to their respective secret mantras.
The secret mantra of Maheśvara is:
"Oṃ arśaniye svāhā. The secret mantra of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, is:
"Oṃ acyutadhara ya svāhā. The secret mantra of Agni, the Fire God, is:
"Oṃ agunaye svāhā. The secret mantra of King Yama is:
"Oṃ yamayai svāhā. The secret mantra of the rākṣasas is:
"Oṃ rākṣasādhipataye svāhā. The secret mantra of the nāgas and water deities is:
"Oṃ varuṇa svāhā. The secret mantra of all the wind deities is:
"Oṃ vāyavi svāhā. The secret mantra of all the yakṣas is:
"Oṃ yakṣabhūtānugrahāya svāhā. Furthermore, the secret mantra for bestowing [benefits] upon all classes of spirits and ghosts in this region is:

"Guhyastambha guhyastambha viśācanāṃ svāhā | Kuṅkuṅbudhanāṃ svāhā. Having performed the ritual offerings as described above, one should wash the hands and rinse the mouth, re-enter the maṇḍala, prostrate to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and perform the recitation as usual.
"Next, the ritual for entering the maṇḍala and conferring empowerment upon the Vajra-disciples is explained.

That Ācārya, having previously received the complete empowerment ritual from his master according to the Dharma, and clearly understanding the rules of the samaya, should possess the mastery of the Ācārya’s methods and regulations; such a person should make this request and must fully observe the proper deportment."
Conceiving of the teacher as a Tathāgata, he joined his palms in reverence, prostrated with his head at the teacher’s feet, pressed his hands against the teacher’s feet, and spoke these words:
“Venerable One, you are indeed the Tathāgata; you are indeed Vajradhara.”
I now take refuge in the Venerable One and seek to train for the sake of perfect enlightenment; for the sake of purifying my vajra-nature, I seek to train in the discipline of pure ethical conduct.
I pray that the Venerable One will compassionately accept me, just as the most excellent sons [of the Buddha] do not abandon any sentient being who possesses the seed of enlightenment.

I have now awakened the bodhicitta; desiring to establish myself in the stage of non-retrogression, I seek entry into the maṇḍala. I pray only that the Venerable One will compassionately instruct me, so that I may see it in its entirety.

May I receive the empowerment conferred by all Buddhas in concert; may I be invested with the vajra-jewel-lotus karma; and may all the supreme and wondrous matters contained within the Great Section be fully gathered and bestowed upon me, so that my body and mind may be purified, my wisdom made lucid, and all profound meanings within both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna be spontaneously understood.

Regarding all the Brahmā devas, Śakra, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and other deities, as well as their retinues of spirits, yakṣas, kiṃnarīs, and so forth—for the sake of benefiting and bringing all sentient beings to maturity, and to bestow peace and happiness upon them—I pray that I may be able to utterly subdue their power.

May I and all sentient beings attain liberation from birth and death and reach the state of nirvana, becoming like those noble ones who, endowed with the primary and secondary marks, enter the rank of the Tathāgatas.
"How may this be attained?
We pray that the Ācārya will compassionately instruct us.
The Ācārya, knowing that the disciple is capable of receiving the supreme Dharma, should say:
"As you have requested, I shall now bestow [this] upon you according to the Buddha’s instructions; you should listen with single-minded attention and let your mind not be distracted.
If your mind is distracted, you will not be empowered by all the Tathāgatas and Vajrasattva."
"Next, instruct them to confess their transgressions openly, causing them to call out their own names:
'I, [Name], from beginningless kalpas until now, have extensively committed immeasurable and boundless sins with my body, speech, and mind.'"
Now, before all the Buddhas, I confess and repent with a sincere heart, not daring to conceal anything.
As I now repent, I vow never to commit such acts again; may my transgressions be extinguished, as fully described in the extensive texts.

I rejoice in all those two kinds of profound and difficult-to-enter provisions, immeasurable merits, and the bringing of benefit and happiness to all the world by those Tathāgatas and their spiritual heirs.
"Next, have them take refuge in the Three Jewels:
'The Teachers of Gods and Humans upon lotus seats of all families, Who have attained great liberation and transcended the three realms,
Whose merit is perfected and who possess great compassion— To all of you, I take refuge with a sincere heart.'"

The dwelling place of those with supreme wisdom, which those of inferior vehicles fear as a dense forest, can swiftly extinguish the existence of birth and death; I now take refuge in this most excellent Dharma.
Able to remove the snake venom of greed, hatred, and delusion, Who by means of wisdom escapes the house of birth and death—
To that Great Compassionate One who awakens others, I pay homage and take refuge in the Honored One among the multitudes.
"Next, instruct them to resolve upon Bodhicitta:
'Listen with single-minded attention:

Bodhicitta arises from Great Compassion; it is the primary cause for attaining Buddhahood and the root of wisdom. It can destroy the karmic retribution of ignorance and can utterly crush the enmity of Māra.'"
Since you have been able to give rise to the great bodhicitta, you should now make a great vow through the union of mind and speech.
Repeat these words after me:

"I, [Name], for the sake of rescuing and liberating all sentient beings, have given rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta; regarding the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the gates of the Dharma up to the six pāramitās, I vow to fulfill them and practice them without interruption."

I dedicate all the roots of goodness I have accumulated to all sentient beings. May I and all sentient beings together realize this profound Dharma-gate; may our minds be pure and vast like space; may we, through effortless mastery, be able to accomplish immeasurable Buddha-deeds; and by means of impartial great compassion and various skillful means, may we tame and benefit all sentient beings, leading them all to enter the nirvana without remainder.
"Regarding the Buddha’s ten powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma), may I and all sentient beings together attain them all.

Having thus instructed them, he had the disciples sit each according to their seniority and rank in order, remaining with palms joined, their minds pure, respectful, and free from distraction or agitation.
The master may empower a thread with secret mantras and tie it around his left arm, or use scented unguents, or employ mental visualization; by means of these secret mantras, he protects him.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ mahāvajrakavaca-jaya-vajri kuru vajrakārya vajra vajra haṃ. Next, having applied this secret mantra to the fragrant ointment, smear it upon the palms of all the disciples.
The secret mantra says:
*Oṃ vajra-gandhe dhūpya svāhā*. At the time of applying the incense, one addresses the disciples, saying:
"May you all fully attain the fragrance of the morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas."
Next, having added fragrant white flowers with the secret mantra, hold them and bestow the secret mantra, saying:
"Oṃ vajra puṣpe oṃ. Then speak thus:
"May you obtain the thirty-two marks of a Great Man (mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa) of all Tathāgatas."
"Next, holding an incense burner, apply this secret mantra to fumigate the disciple’s two hands.
The secret mantra is:
*Oṃ vajra dhūpe dhūpa āḥ*. Having spoken thus:"
"May you obtain the wondrous complexion nourished by the great compassion of all Tathāgatas.
Having thus empowered the lamp with this secret mantra, he causes the disciple to gaze upon it.
The secret mantra says:
"Oṃ vajrarucaye prabhāsa. Thus he spoke:
"May you all obtain the light of wisdom of all Tathāgatas."

"Next, using the secret mantra of the aforementioned ritual for smiling, one adds the branches of trees such as the udumbara and aśvattha to serve as tooth-sticks; furthermore, one empowers those tooth-sticks with the secret mantra of the vajra-sword of the profound wisdom of all Buddhas, which destroys the afflictions and secondary afflictions of all sentient beings."

"Furthermore, have the disciple take the flowers received in their palms and offer them to the foremost and most honored among all the Tathāgata families. Next, hand over the tooth-stick; the master should mark it for himself so as not to err, and have the disciple chew it while facing east."

"Having finished washing and rinsing, one should discard the chewed tooth-stick (dantakāṣṭha) facing [the teacher]. The master should observe the direction toward which the tip of the tooth-stick points.

Taking the end that was chewed as the head, whichever direction it points toward is generally its corresponding family (kula)—if it points toward the four intermediate directions, it is generally the Vairocana family;
if it stands upright, one should know this to be an extremely auspicious sign."
Once the teacher has completed his observation, he should bestow [instruction] upon his disciples and, according to their respective dispositions, address them as follows:
"Each of you should straighten your mind and maintain mindfulness; having paid homage to the Buddhas, bind your minds to sleep and seek the signs of the objective realm."
"Whatever you have seen, come in the morning and recount it in full.
Having given this instruction, he allowed him to depart as he pleased.
In the morning, he went to his teacher and related his dream exactly as it had occurred.

If one’s sensory objects are inverted and filled with many discursive thoughts, this is a sign of impurity; one should take the five products of the cow—namely, milk, curd, clarified butter, dung, and urine—and after mixing them together and purifying them by straining, empower them by reciting the Vajra-mantra twenty-one times and administer them for consumption.
If the body and mind are purified, take white sandalwood water and, using the Vajra Secret Mantra twenty-one times, have them drink it.
The mantra is: "Oṃ vajrodaka ṭha.

Once they have drunk it according to the ritual, at the end of the night, lead them outside the door of the maṇḍala chamber and instruct them to confess all karmic obstacles and to rejoice in and dedicate all merits.

"Having instructed them in the four types of prostration as described above, take a red robe and mantle; according to the method for donning the *kāṣāya*, if they are renunciants, they should wear robes of *gandha* color. Then, cover their eyes with a piece of red silk and instruct them to form the *vajrasattva* mudrā, while orally transmitting this heart-mantra three times."
The secret mantra says:

“Samaya satvaṃ. Then, instruct [the disciple] to join the two fingers—the ring finger and the little finger—upright like a needle, and hang various white flower garlands or garlands of various fragrant flowers upon that needle. Next, lead [the disciple] into the entrance of the maṇḍala and confer this secret mantra three times:
“Samaya hūṃ. One should then say to them:
"You have now entered the family of the retinue of all Tathāgatas; I shall now cause you to give birth to vajra-wisdom.
You should know that by means of this wisdom, you shall attain the siddhi-activities of all Tathāgatas."
Furthermore, you must not explain these ritual matters to anyone who has not entered such maṇḍalas;
if you should so speak, you will not only violate your samaya but will also bring calamity upon yourself.
The master should form the *sattvavajra-mudrā* with his fingers extended, place it upon the disciple’s crown, and declare:
“This is the *samaya-vajra-mudrā*. If you should ever speak of this to anyone who has not yet entered the maṇḍala, it shall cause your head to split asunder.”
"Do not give rise to doubt or arrogance toward me; you should instead develop deep reverence and faith.
You should regard my person as that of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, and you must fully carry out all that I instruct."
If you do not act thus, you will bring calamity upon yourself, perhaps meeting an untimely death and falling into hell; therefore, you must be cautious.
Having given this instruction, you should now entreat all the Tathāgatas for their protection, so that Vajrasattva may enter your body and mind.
The master then again binds the Vajrasattva mudrā and declares:
"This is the Samaya-vajra, named Vajrasattva; may it enter your body to become the unsurpassed vajra-wisdom."
Recite this secret mantra:

“Vajra-piśāca vajra-piśācā. Next, form the Wrathful Vajra Fist, hooking the two fingers of the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (little) fingers together, and recite the hundred-syllable secret mantra of the Mahāyāna Samaya.
Having uttered this with vajra speech, he releases the upper mudrā; by the power and efficacy of this secret mantra, he causes the disciple to enter vajra-wisdom and realize sublime insight.

"By means of this wisdom, one is able to fully attain the realization of the various mental states of all sentient beings; one can know the activities of the three periods of time within the world; one can make the bodhicitta firm; one can extinguish all suffering and affliction; one can be free from all fears; no evil whatsoever can cause harm; one is sustained by the collective empowerment of all Tathāgatas; all siddhis appear before one; and all unprecedented, peaceful, and supreme matters are obtained spontaneously without being sought."

"You should consider yourself deeply fortunate; I shall now briefly explain for you the superior qualities of merit. By means of this Dharma, you shall attain all stages, samādhis, dhāraṇīs, supernormal powers, samāpattis, pāramitās, powers, and fearlessnesses. Furthermore, the profound meanings of hundreds of thousands of sūtras that you have never before seen or heard will naturally become understood."
"You shall soon realize for yourself the true wisdom of all Buddhas; how much more so the other, inferior siddhis?
Having spoken these words, he asked:
"What kind of realm have you seen?"
If one sees a white sign, they should be taught the wisdom of the supreme siddhi;
if one sees a yellow sign, they should be taught the wisdom of the siddhi arising from the principles of meaning;
if one sees a red sign, they should be taught the wisdom of the siddhi of service and offering.
If one sees a black sign, one should teach the wisdom of *abhicāru-siddhi*;
if one sees a variegated color, one should teach the wisdom of all *karma-siddhi*.

If no auspicious signs are seen, this constitutes an obstacle of sin; one should then employ the *pāśa-pāpa-vidhna-mudrā* to hook those various sins, and further employ the *sarva-pāpa-vināśana-mudrā* to destroy them.
The *Āṅkuśapāpa-sūtra* states:

"Having formed the vajra-bind, extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers as a needle; bend the *vīrya* and *prajñā* fingers to form the shape of a *vajra-jaṅgha* (vajra-thigh) upon the backs of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers, ensuring they do not touch one another. Furthermore, visualize the syllable *yaṃ* at the tips of the *vīrya* and *prajñā* fingers, and with the hook, drag out all the karmic obstacles and sins within that person's body."

Recite this secret mantra: *Oṃ sarvabāpākaliśane viśodhana samaya vajra hūṃ raṅ*. While reciting this mantra, visualize the form of that sin as having the shape of a ghost, black in color with hair standing on end. Then, interlace the fingers of both hands, placing the thumbs inside the palms. Visualize that the two fingers of the *vajra-agra* (forefinger) hook and clamp the sin, causing it to enter the palm. Press the faces of the remaining fingers together, then extend the two fingers of the *kṣānti* (ring finger) and *praṇidhāna* (little finger) to form a needle. Visualize the syllable *tra* at the tip of the *praṇidhāna* finger and the syllable *dza* (pronounced *dzhi*) at the tip of the *kṣānti* finger; furthermore, visualize flames arising from above these syllables to seize that sin.
Recite this mantra:

"Oṃ vajra-pāṇi-jñāna-musala-pramardana-sarva-apāya-nigraha-pramokṣaṇa-sarva-āpatti-kṣaya-gati-vinivartana-sarvasattvānāṃ sarvatathāgata-vajrasamayai hūṃ traṭ. Having recited this mantra, apply force by twisting it like the motion of snapping one's fingers, with the right hand above and the left below.
The Treatise says:
"The samaya of all Tathāgatas can liberate all sentient beings from all evil destinies; the Vajradhara should shatter all fetters of the evil destinies."

"Having thus successively crushed those various sins, one further visualizes that the bodies and minds of all Buddhas purify them with their light. The Buddhas of the four directions, such as Akṣobhya, and Vairocana of the zenith, all emit pure light; in the nadir, one visualizes the syllable *Vajrasattva* (the Vajra Hero), which emits wrathful light to utterly destroy [the remaining defilements]."

When performing the ritual in this manner, one will certainly cause them to perceive signs of auspicious realms; it should be known that their karmic obstructions and hindrances are thereby completely extinguished.
"If those karmic obstructions are extremely heavy such that no auspicious sign appears, the master should recite for them the *tathatā-gāthā* (verses of reality) to bring about their awakening.
The verse says:
"The Dharmakāya of Samantabhadra pervades all; He is the sovereign lord of the world."
Without beginning or end, without birth or cessation, its nature and characteristics are eternally abiding, equal to space.
The mind possessed by all sentient beings is the firm bodhi, named *sattva*;
when this mind dwells unmoving in *samādhi* with diligent resolve, it is named *vajra*.

I now speak these words of truth: I pray that the World-Honored One will uphold his original vow, grant all *siddhis* for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, and through compassion and pity, bestow empowerment.
Having spoken these verses, he again formed the Vajra-entrance mudrā and recited the secret mantra of the syllable *A* one hundred and eight times.
The Sūtra states:

"Form the Vajra-bond; with the wisdom-finger (*jñāna-aṅguli*) and the concentration-finger (*samādhi-aṅguli*), pinch the base joint of the thumb (*dāna-aṅguli*) and the wisdom-finger (*prajñā-aṅguli*); with the effort-finger (*vīrya-aṅguli*), slightly curve them so that they support one another. This is it.

"Once these rites have been performed in this manner, one should again question them; if no auspicious signs appear, they may only be led in to receive the samaya, but one must not confer the empowerment upon them."
Next, one should confer this secret mantra three times:

"Oṃ pratisarāyā vajra hoḥ. Having recited this, instruct them to cast the garland they were wearing into the center of the maṇḍala. According to their past karma, wherever the garland lands, have them immediately recite the secret mantra of that particular family; it should be known that they will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, again bestow this secret mantra three times, and cause the disciple to release the *samaya* mudrā he has bound upon his heart.
The mantra says:
*Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra-niṣīda dṛḍho me bhava sarva-siddhiṃ me prayaccha hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ.* The commentary states:
"May the Vajra remain eternally firm and steadfast; may it empower my mind and grant me all *siddhis*.
Then, taking the flower garland that was thrown, he adds this secret mantra: "Oṃ pratisaṃharāśvasta-vakre-mahāsattva mahābala. The commentary states:
"May the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta grant you his protection.

While reciting these secret words, he should immediately bind that garland upon the person's head; by virtue of binding the garland, they will receive the protection of the Mahāsattva and swiftly accomplish all supreme siddhis.
"Next, recite this mantra to remove the cloth covering the eyes. The mantra says:

*Oṃ vajrasattva sarvavidye ti vīra vikurva cakṣuḥ udghāṭaya udghāṭaya pravaratā udghāṭaya sarvākṣiṇi vajracakṣuḥ anuttara he vajravaiśya paśya maṇḍalam.* The Commentary states: "The phrase *sarvavidye* means 'all-knowing. *Ti* means 'for you. *Vīra* means 'hero. *Vikurva* means 'manifest your power. *Cakṣuḥ* means 'eye. *Udghāṭaya udghāṭaya* means 'open, open! *Pravaratā* means 'supreme. *Udghāṭaya* means 'cause it to be opened. *Sarvākṣiṇi* means 'all eyes. *Vajracakṣuḥ* means 'Vajra-eye. *Anuttara* means 'unsurpassed. *He* is an address. *Vajravaiśya* means 'O Vajra-merchant. *Paśya maṇḍalam* means 'behold the mandala.'"
Vajrasattva himself has personally and exclusively opened for you the five eyes and the unsurpassed Vajra-eye.
Next, call the disciple and show them everywhere the various signs and characteristics of the deities within the maṇḍala.

By virtue of this dharma, one is protected and sustained by all Tathāgatas; Vajrasattva dwells constantly within one’s heart, and whatever is sought shall be obtained, even up to the attainment of the body of a Vajradhara, until one gradually enters into the dharmic nature of the essence of all Tathāgatas.
"Next is the initiation for the disciples.

The initiation maṇḍala should be located outside the eastern gate of the great maṇḍala, extending downward for two cubits (*hasta*). It should be drawn with white powder as a perfect square, with a single gate opening on one side. Within the four corners, draw images of Vajrapāṇi: in the direction of Īśāna, named 'Abiding in Non-Conceptualization' (*niṣprapañca-vihārin*);
in the corner of the direction of Agni, named 'Stainless Space' (*ākāśa-vimala*)."
In the direction of the Rākṣasas, there is one named Viśuddhanetra;
in the direction of the Vāyudevas, there is one named Nānāvidhacitravastradhara.

In the center, paint a great lotus flower with eight petals, complete with a calyx and filaments; outside the flower, encircle it with the form of a lunar disc, from which rays of light radiate outward.

"In the square [mandala], paint four bodhisattvas on the four petals, each riding upon the power of their former vows' excellence—the one on the petal of the Indra direction is named Dhāraṇīśvararāja;
the one in the Yama direction is named Samyaksmṛtyudgata;
and the one in the Nāga direction is named Satvārtharati."
In the direction of the yakṣas is the one named Mahākaruṇika.
On the petals of the four corners, one should paint the Four Messengers: in the direction of Īśāna is the one named Vardhamānaviśeṣacaryā;
in the direction of Agni is the one named Pūrṇamanoratha.
In the direction of the Rākṣasas, there is the name "Non-Attachment";
in the direction of the Vāyudevas, there is the name "Supreme Liberation.

On the flower pedestal, one should visualize the meaning of the syllable *a* as previously described; upon this syllable *a*, one should visualize a single circular dot, which signifies the meaning of the Dharmakāya Nirvāṇa of True Suchness (tathatā) in its perfect stillness. All other offerings, banners, flowers, and adornments are to be arranged exactly according to the ritual procedures of the Great Maṇḍala.
One should form this thought:
"I now perform the consecration for the sake of the son of good family [Name]; I pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas descend to this ritual arena and accept my offerings."

"Clearly visualize that the invited assembly of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas has all gathered together; then, move the precious vases from within the great maṇḍala and place them in their respective corners according to their original directions.

Furthermore, visualize four wheels outside the boundary surrounding the maṇḍala, and have four pure attendants hold the aforementioned precious vases while standing within moon-discs: the person in the direction of Śakra should be visualized as Samantabhadra; the person in the direction of Yama as Maitreya; the person in the direction of the Nāgas as Sarvavighnaghātaka; and the person in the direction of the Yakṣas as Sarvadurgatipariśodhana."

Then, lead the one who has received initiation into the gate of the direction of Śakra; have them sit upon a lotus pedestal and make offerings with various kinds of flowers, unguents, incense, oil lamps, banners, canopies, and sublime music. If these cannot be prepared, perform the offerings according to one's ability.
The reason for this is that such a person sits upon the seat of a Buddha.
Furthermore, by means of various songs and hymns of praise, one causes them to give rise to a profound and deep heart of joy.
He spoke this verse:
"When the Buddhas descend from Tuṣita, Śakra, Brahmā, nāgas, and spirits attend them in service;
May you now obtain all such various, supreme, wondrous, and auspicious matters."
Born in the palace of the Śākyas in Kapilavastu, The Dragon Kings showered him with the water of nectar;
As the various devas made offerings for his auspicious rites, May your consecration likewise be so.
Upon the vajra seat for the sake of all sentient beings, In the final watch of the night, you subdue Māra and attain perfect enlightenment;
Manifesting all manner of rare and auspicious events, May you fully accomplish this very seat.
In the groves of Vārāṇasī, you adorned the place and opened the wondrous Dharma for the five sages;
having accomplished immeasurable auspicious deeds, may you now fully realize them all.
"If there are further praises, one may compose them as desired to inspire superior resolve and give rise to beneficial joy.
Next, one should confer upon them the empowerment."
First, visualize that at the crown of the disciple’s head is the syllable *A*, topped with a bindu, the meaning of which is as explained previously.
From this syllable, rays of light and flame are emitted, blazing and resplendent.

Furthermore, visualize within the disciple’s heart a lunar disc, inside of which is an eight-petaled lotus; upon its pedestal is also the syllable *A*. If one has attained the Vajra family, visualize a *vajra* within the syllable *A*.
In the Ratnakula there is the jewel;
in the Padmakula, the lotus;
and in the Karmakula, the karmavajra.
In the Vairocana family, one should visualize a stūpa.

The master should visualize himself as an image of Vairocana and take the family flask obtained for the disciple—the Tathāgata family flask. If it is a mandala of painted images, place it wherever there is space;

if it is a mandala of hand seals (*mudrā*), place it upon the mandala. Visualize the substance of that particular family within the water of the flask—such as a *vajra* jewel, and so forth—and have the disciple form the seal of their respective family. Place it upon the disciple’s head, recite the secret mantra of that family seven times, and perform the consecration.
The secret mantra of the Vajra Family is:
Oṃ vajrasattvābhiṣiñca hūṃ. The secret mantra of the Ratna Family is:
Oṃ vajraratnābhiṣiñca traḥ. The secret mantra of the Padma Family is:
"Oṃ vajradharmābhiṣiñca hrīḥ. The secret mantra of the Karma family is:
"Oṃ vajrakarmābhiṣiñca āḥ. One should visualize the syllable *la* upon the forehead, its appearance like gold;
one should visualize the syllable *ra* with a vowel-sign (*u*) above each of the two eyes, its color like fire, from which flames arise upward.
Between his two feet, one should visualize various colors forming the mark of a Dharma wheel, adorned with the eight blessings.

Next, recite the secret mantra of the Sattvavajra heart; having added scented ointment, apply it to his chest. The reason for performing this rite of empowerment is to cause the disciple to become a Vajrasattva.

"Next, having performed the ritual for placing the seals at the five locations on the head as described above, one should again form the Vairocana seal and recite the root mantra. Having placed it upon his heart, then his throat, and then the crown of his head, one should then clearly visualize all the Tathāgatas bestowing their supreme secret empowerment upon his head. Thereupon, one should form the four types of garlands as described and bind them to his forehead according to the specific rites of each family."

"If one performs the ritual for the Ācārya consecration, one should follow the sequence as in the aforementioned method, employing all five vases and binding four types of garlands around the forehead in successive order."
"Having done this, lead him outside the mandala, change his damp garments, and have him put on clean clothes.
If he is a kṣatriya or a householder, have him wear his usual upper garment; then place a small low stool inside the mandala to serve as a cushion for his dampness."

Once they have been led in and seated, the master takes a five-pronged *vajra* with feathers attached and places it in their two hands, while employing various skillful means of speech to instruct, inspire, and comfort them.
He spoke these verses for him:
“The ritual of the Vajra Empowerment of all Buddhas— You have already received this empowerment according to the Dharma.
In order to accomplish the nature of the Tathāgata, You should receive this vajra.”
Having spoken this verse, he recited the secret mantra:
*Oṃ vajra-nairātmye svabhāva-śuddhe tvaṃ abhiṣiñca me tiṣṭha vajrasamaye siddhya tvaṃ samaya*. The commentary states:
"You have now been consecrated and have attained the status of the Vajra Lord. This vajra shall abide permanently within you as your *samaya*."
"Furthermore, take up the vajra; if it belongs to the Ratna family, one should again visualize a jewel upon the vajra;
the other families follow this pattern."
When reciting the preceding verse, one should change the word "vajra" in the first line to "maṇi";
all other families should be modified accordingly.
Next, prefix the disciple's actual name with the word "vajra" and address them by that name, while reciting this mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasattva maṃ hūṃ | abhiṣiñce 'bhiṣekaya vajranāma viśvakarman | vajranāma [Name]! The commentary states: "I have completed the conferral of initiation upon you;
I bestow upon you a name by means of a Vajra-name, and your name is Vajra-[Name]."
"If it is a mantra of another family (kula), one adds [the name of] a jewel, a lotus, or the like to form the name and calls it by that.
If the person has received the dharma of an ācārya, they shall simply use the name of the family from which they originally obtained [the initiation]."
If you wish to change the old name, you may choose any excellent name from among the various *pāramitās* according to your preference.

Furthermore, having made offerings of incense, flowers, and various ritual implements to the one who has received the empowerment, the master should take a small golden vajra and, as in the rite for treating the eyes, wipe both of [the disciple's] eyes while addressing him thus:
"O son of noble family!..."

Just as the Physician-King of the world can cure cataracts of the eye, so too do the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, today remove the cataract of ignorance for you; this is done so that you may give rise to the eye of wisdom and perceive the true reality of all phenomena.
"Next, he again takes up a mirror and causes him to gaze into it, explaining for him the nature and characteristics of all phenomena.
He speaks this verse:
"The nature of all phenomena Is such that neither defilement nor purity can be found."
Neither real nor unreal, all manifest from causes and conditions.
You should know that all phenomena have no basis in their own nature;
you are now a true son of the Buddha and should extensively benefit sentient beings.
"Next, having taken up the vajra, the master should generate a sense of reverence toward the disciple—thinking, 'This person is capable of continuing the lineage of all Buddhas.
The master should then bestow a conch shell upon him and address him thus:
'From this day forward, you shall turn the Wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas.'"
You shall blow the unsurpassed Dharma conch, causing the sound of the Great Dharma to pervade all places; you should not give rise to doubt or fear regarding this teaching.
As for the ultimate purity of all secret words and the principles of practice, you should extensively and skillfully reveal them to sentient beings.
"Good son, listen attentively:
if one can act in this way, all Tathāgatas know that this person is able to repay the Buddha's kindness.
Therefore, at all times and in all places, you shall be protected by all Vajradharas, who will bring you peace and happiness."
"Next, one should lead them forward to the great maṇḍala and explain the samaya to them, causing it to become firm.
One should say:
'O son of noble family!'"
You should steadfastly uphold the True Dharma; even if you encounter oppression, affliction, or even the threat of death, you must not abandon the cultivation of the bodhicitta.
You should not be stingy toward those who seek the Dharma, nor should you perform even the slightest act that is harmful to sentient beings.
This is the supreme meaning of the words, the sphere of the noble ones' practice.
I have now fully explained it for you; you should accordingly practice in accordance with what has been taught.
The disciple should rejoice and, with palms joined at the crown of his head, accept it.
Furthermore, [the master] takes a five-pronged vajra and hands it to him, saying:
"This is the vajra held in the hand of Vajrasattva, the essential nature of all Buddhas; you should firmly protect the prohibitive precepts and always maintain and carry it."
"Once the disciple has received [the initiation], he should be made to recite this essential vow of the secret mantra (*samaya-mantra*).
The secret mantra is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhi-vajrasamayatistha tiṣṭha eṣo 'haṃ tvām dārayāmi vajrasattva hī hī hī hūṃ.*" The commentary states:
"May the Vajrasattva-samaya of all Tathāgatas abide within me; I shall always protect it.
Having performed this rite, the teacher should instruct [the disciple] in all the secret samaya-wisdom of the maṇḍala.
If a disciple should fail or lose the samaya-mudrā, the master should restrain them so that it is not destroyed.
The disciple should be respectful and honor the master, never looking for their faults;
they should harbor no mutual resentment toward their fellow students.
One should say to them:
"You must always give rise to compassion for all sentient beings, showing them pity and instruction; do not harbor weariness or aversion.
Then, one should speak these verses:
“The most grievous sin in the three realms Is none other than lack of revulsion;
Regarding the objects of desire, You should give rise to a mind of revulsion.”
"Desiring to cause his disciples to maintain [the precepts] with joy, he spoke these verses for them:
"These samayas have been taught to you by all the Buddhas;
Maintain and cherish them well, as you would protect your own life."
"Once the disciple has received the teacher’s instruction, he should prostrate at the teacher’s feet and say:
'As you have instructed me, I vow to practice accordingly.

Furthermore, for the sake of those disciples who have already received initiation—in order to bring them to perfection in the dharma of tranquility and to eliminate their calamities and obstacles—one should perform the homa rite for them."

In the fire-god direction (*āgneyī*) of the consecration mandala, one must not interrupt [the ritual]; rather, one should construct it at a distance of four cubits (*hasta*), with the altar being one span (*vitasti*) high.
In its center, one should excavate a *kuṇḍa* (fire-pit) with a circular diameter of one cubit and a depth of twelve finger-breadths (*aṅgula*), carefully smoothing it with clean clay.
Construct two layers of rafters; the inner rafters shall each be one finger-breadth in height and width, while the outer rafters shall each be four finger-breadths in height and width.
The base must be perfectly level and upright. Upon this base, fashion an image of Śiva and Vajra, with the handle extending toward the south, resembling the shape of the worldly letter "T" (丁).
The handle is four finger-widths long and four finger-widths wide; its crossbar is eight finger-widths long, with both height and width being four finger-widths each.
Outside of this, construct an earthen platform shaped like a lotus leaf.

Next, outside [the inner area], arrange the seating for the officiating masters; surround the *juncha* with *kuśa* grass to serve as the seating for the noble assembly. Sprinkle purified scented water and spread the grass while sprinkling water, performing all actions in a clockwise direction.
"Those who should be given ghee, curd, milk, honey, milk-rice, cakes, and fruits—these consist of the five grains, namely: rice, grain, mung beans, sesame, and wheat."
Take branches of the *śrīvṛkṣa* tree for firewood; if such trees are unavailable, take those with white sap as a substitute, such as the *śamī* or *udumbara*.
Cut them evenly and short, separately selecting small branches about the size of a thumb, twelve finger-breadths in length, numbering one hundred and eight.

"Place the clarified butter, grain, and firewood together on the right side of the altar—if one cannot carve a *kuṇḍa*, then draw its shape in red—positioning the hearth in the center; the rest is as described above."

The master sits facing north, and the disciples kneel in a row to his left. Taking either previously consecrated fire or fire produced by a new drill, he places two sets of scented water upon the altar—one for offering to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and one for offering to the Fire Deity (Agni).

Having sprinkled the water to perform the purification (*śauca*), and having placed it within the *kuṇḍa* (fire pit), he recites this mantra three times: *Namo samantavajrāṇāṃ tadyathā jvala mahālohitaspharaṇe hūṃ haṃ maṃ.* Having recited this mantra three times, he sprinkles pure water upon the fire, as well as upon the *darbha* grass and all other offering implements.
"Next, light the fire; do not blow upon it with your mouth, but fan it with an object.
Take white sandalwood paste and smear it all over the *kundika* (incense burner), and scatter white fragrant flowers around the four sides of the platform."
Within the flames, one should visualize the syllable RAṂ, which transforms into the Fire God (Agni), white in color with yellow hair, three-eyed and four-armed:
his two right hands hold a *kunta* spear and a staff;
his two left hands—

First, assume the gesture of fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) by stepping forward and extending the palm; with the palm facing outward, hold the beads of the rosary between the fingers—visualize that the body of the Fire Deity (*Agni-deva*) is entirely enveloped in flames.

"Next, holding an incense burner, invite the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; the ritual for the invitation is as explained in the Great Maṇḍala. Visualize clearly that all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas come to the assembly and sit upon the auspicious grass (śarīra)."
The master observed the feathers and assumed a fearless posture; he held the feathers at his wrist so that they resembled an armlet.
He then summoned the Fire Deity and recited this secret mantra:

"Oṃ ajñātaye nibhikṣaṇi bhayaṃ nivāśiviraḥ sarvasamagrahiṃ tvaṃ āhuti mahāraṇāsamin saṃnihe tu bhava | Oṃ ajñātaye he bibhikṣe bhaṅga bhāṇaye nibhayaṃ svāhā. While reciting this mantra, visualize that the Fire Deity (Agnideva) arrives and enters the body as previously visualized; then, sprinkle water from the perfumed water vessel upon your hands and onto the fire.

"Next, take hold of the sacrificial ladle and pour three ladles each of clarified butter, milk, honey, and other such substances into the fire to offer to the Fire Deity; alternatively, it is also permissible to mix them together in one place and pour three ladles."
At the time of the offering, recite this mantra once for every ladleful. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ āgaccha āye svāhā*.

The Master, holding the vajra with his left hand and the hook with his right, [invokes] the disciple’s wisdom through the perfection of insight (*prajñāpāramitā*). Separately, using a small ladle as before, he pours the offering into the fire twenty-one times for each person. As each ladleful is offered, they should single-mindedly contemplate all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the Fire God (*Agni*), joyfully reciting the secret mantras of the five families according to their respective lineages—one mantra for each ladleful—as an act of worship.
If one wishes to eliminate calamities, recite this mantra:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | amoghaśrīpāragate mahāśāntagarakarapariśramadharmeniryāta-sphoṭa-buddhadharma-samanta-pratāpa svāhā. Each disciple should perform it accordingly; if the ācārya performs the rite, he should recite it up to one hundred and eight times.

Furthermore, having mixed together ghee, oil, milk, honey, and so forth, one should ladle them with a small spoon one hundred and eight times, pouring them into the fire as an offering; for each ladle, one should recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the Mahāyāna Samaya once.

"If you wish to separately make offerings to the various bodhisattvas and others, you should each recite their respective heart-mantras—either twenty-one or forty-nine times, or as many times as you wish—and pour [the substances] over them. Then, take one hundred and eight small sticks, pierce both ends of each stick with ghee and honey, and offer them into the fire from time to time."

"Once the ritual procedures have been performed, one should next make offerings and provide gifts to the devas, spirits, and their retinues located outside the eight directions behind the aforementioned seats, following the previous method of reciting the secret mantras while pouring libations into the fire."

Having performed this, the master emerges to wash his hands, returns to his original seat, and after making the three ladlefuls of offering to the fire deity as before, addresses the disciple, saying:

"You have now fully received the empowerment ritual (*abhiṣeka*). Even if one were to provide all manner of worldly offerings, they would not equal the merit of personally making offerings to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; you should each give rise to such a mind."

After causing each of his disciples to make their own vows, the master should take a censer in hand and make offerings throughout to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the Fire Deity; he should then recite the secret mantras to request them to return to their original abodes.
Immediately rising from his seat, he proceeded to the position at the great mandala and addressed the disciples, saying:
"For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, the Buddhas have taught this sublime Dharma of the excellent field of merit."
"You should each prepare incense and flowers according to your means to make offerings to the great assembly; this will enable you to obtain immeasurable karmic rewards.
Furthermore, in order to make offerings to all Tathāgatas and the hosts of the Vajra Family, you should perform the offering as described above using the Karma-mudrā and the Samaya-mudrā.
Furthermore, having performed the four kinds of secret offerings through the secret mantra of vajra-praise, one recites this verse:
“By the grace of Vajrasattva, I have attained the supreme Vajra-jewel;
Now, with this vajra-dharma song, May you perform for me the vajra-activity.”
"Furthermore, perform the secret offering ritual with the *vajra-nṛtya* (vajra-dance) *añjali* and the *vajra-hāsya* (vajra-laughter), among others.
Next, having made offerings of incense and flowers with one's hands to the holy assembly of the outer maṇḍala, one should address the disciples, saying:
'Each of you should, according to your respective capacity, make offerings to the Buddhas.'"

When they have completed the performance of the offerings, in order to protect the bodies of their disciples, they should each distribute a small portion of the flowers, incense, fruits, cakes, and so forth that were requested from and offered to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to those disciples.
He further commanded them to take a solemn oath as previously stated, that they must not speak of this Dharma casually.
Having given these instructions, he had the disciples each return to their original positions.

The master, having performed the recitation and offerings of praise according to his ability as usual, shall then request the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and their retinues within the maṇḍala to return to their original lands.

He shall then erect the *sattvavajra-mudrā* and recite this secret mantra: *Oṃ kṛtva-jaya-sarvasattvārtha-siddhi-nidhāna-ye-tadanugamya-sthāna-buddha-viśuddhe punarāgamanāya oṃ vajrasattva muḥ.* The commentary states:
Having already accomplished this supreme benefit and bestowed it upon all sentient beings, I pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas return to their own lands.
If I should again invoke you, I pray that you will descend once more.
"This mudrā and mantra are used in all maṇḍalas for requesting the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the retinues of all families to return to their original abodes.
*The Vajraśekhara Yoga Sūtra: A Brief Extract on Recitation*, Scroll Four.
